"It's still very young, less than a year old. Being given away twice in a single day might cause psychological issues," the junior student reminded from the side.

chunks.chineseText:
鹦鹉心理问题实际上很多的，很多时候是认定一个主人的，有的还会有分离焦虑，会自己拔掉羽毛，自残。

宋郁动摇了。

但他还是不确定，养育是要负责的，自己不就是……被弃养的么？

他有什么能力——

肩头一重，圆滚滚的鸟飞了过来，鸟头歪了歪，似乎是在看。

宋郁下巴是有些瘦削的，黑沉沉的眸子里有了些“水纹”，犹如一个镜子，倒映出来一只小鸟。

“它喜欢你。”

师弟再次这么说道。

白粼粼：“……”

谁问你了！我说谁问你了！

鸟头一转，短喙上下一张，眼看着就要骂人了。

师弟提前模仿：“啾啾啾啾。”

青年后面甚至还吹了个口哨。

鸟要气死了，毛都炸了起来，蹦跶了两下，决心起飞去叨那人一口。

但又被宋郁给握住了。

“。”

白粼粼被放到了岛台上，宋郁面色有些苍白，但还是一字一句解释：

“可我养不好你。”

“我不懂鸟类的习性，这样是不负责的。”

宋郁觉得自己仍然昏昏沉沉的，他本来就有病，手指里的血管像是在跳，一阵阵地刺痛。

直到一个软软的爪子扣了上来。

白粼粼仰头看了过来。

对视ing。

师弟觉得有意思，抬手就把鸟给拨开了，但不到两秒，鸟又蹦跶了回来，还很生气地冲他这边啾了几声。

宋郁愣住了。

齐思扬微微挑眉，看着自己师弟又拨开一次，鸟气得毛都炸了，但还是执着地又去上宋郁的手。

“哈哈它好喜欢你。”

白粼粼直接尬住了。

“。”

炸毛了半天，窝窝囊囊的。

但或许是这句话真起了效果，宋郁后面倒是真的什么也没说了，送走了两位客人。

白粼粼站在人的肩头，很是悠闲地梳理了下羽毛，此战胜利！

夜色如水，岛台那里开了壁灯，暖黄又有氛围感。

就是鸟正好站在灯后面，墙上有巨大的影子，一动一动的，很“威严”。

“啾啾？”

宋郁不知道在想什么，低头发了个短信，通知阿姨晚上不用过来。

他去了厨房，肩头小鸟其实有点重量的，沉沉的，偶尔也能察觉到它在歪头。

打量自己。

有种很微妙的感觉。

宋郁已经独自生活很长时间了，他的私人空间往往只有一个人，但现在多出来……一只鸟。

并且似乎喜欢自己？

宋郁面色苍白，眼睛里一片漆黑，犹如浓墨，他有轻微的躯体化症状。

但现在，却不知道怎么了，没有立即吃药。

反倒是走到橱柜那里，拿出来碟子，给鸟装粮。

他只会做这个……

这算是养吗？

不算。

宋郁怔怔地看着台面上的东西，很乱，有错乱的信息在脑海中碰撞。

[小宋，你妈妈又怀了，这几天你别打电话过去行吗？]

[你也知道不太方便。]

……

[宋郁，我没空管你，又不是我生的，去找你妈。]

[谁的电话啊？阳阳今天吵着要找你呢。]

[哎，宝贝儿，放学了？爸爸抱。]

这些声音有男有女，时而刻薄，时而温和，像是一张张戴着面具的伪人，时时刻刻地吞噬着你的理智。

“啾啾？”

宋郁愣了下，手指冰凉，一下子抽从幻觉中抽离了出来，侧脸有些轻微的痒，他转头看了过去。

鸟头在顶他。

毛绒绒的。

宋郁抬了下手，小鸟脑袋圆滚滚的，又探头看了他一会，才伸出了鸟腿，稳稳地站在了“人工栖杆”上。

碟子里的鸟粮是新的，很小的颗粒，压制工艺很好，几乎没有碎的。

白粼粼被放到了台面上，一阵沉默，非要吃吗？

他仰头看了看少年。

宋郁照旧是没什么大的表情，只是这个距离下，对方腕骨上的痕迹尤为清晰，像是工笔刀划过的……

白粼粼还是有点担忧的。

鸟不能走。

鸟有社会责任感。

他想了想，觉得敷衍吃几口也是可以的，于是低头叨了一口。

咂巴咂巴。

白粼粼觉得有点像麦片，但是又有点青草的味道，有点上头。

又叨了一口。

宋郁垂眸看着，似乎是松了一口气，但又微微皱了皱眉，他总觉得自己忘记了什么。

不过现在已经很晚了。

他打算拿几片面包凑合一下，于是走到了冰箱那里，抬手，拉开冰箱门。

人愣住了。

因为里面简直可以称作“一片混乱”，所有的保鲜膜全部被戳开了，七零八碎的，不止是碗里的卤肉，还有叨了几口的胡萝卜、娃娃菜，就连普通的饮料瓶盖也有齐齐的豁口。

“……”
chunks.englishText:
>
Parrots actually have a lot of psychological issues. Many times they only recognize one owner, and some even suffer from separation anxiety, plucking out their own feathers and self-mutilating.

Song Yu wavered.

But he was still unsure. Raising a pet required responsibility. Wasn't he himself... abandoned?

What capability did he have—

A weight settled on his shoulder. The plump little bird had flown over, tilting its head as if looking at him.

Song Yu's chin was somewhat sharp and slender. His dark, deep eyes rippled with slight "watery rings," like a mirror reflecting a tiny bird.

"It likes you," his junior brother said once more.

Bai Linlin: "..."

*Who asked you! I said, who asked you!*

The bird's head whipped around, its short beak snapping open and shut, looking like it was about to curse him out.

The junior brother mimicked him in advance: "Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp."

The young man even whistled afterward.

The bird was about to die of anger. Its feathers puffed up, and it hopped twice, determined to take flight and peck the guy.

But Song Yu caught it in his hand again.

"."

Bai Linlin was placed onto the kitchen island. Song Yu's face was somewhat pale, but he still explained word by word:

"But I can't raise you well."

"I don't understand the habits of birds. Doing this would be irresponsible."

Song Yu felt like he was still in a daze. He was already sick, and the blood vessels in his fingers felt like they were throbbing, sending waves of sharp pain.

Until a soft little claw gripped him.

Bai Linlin looked up at him.

Staring contest in progress.

The junior brother found this amusing and reached out to brush the bird aside. But in less than two seconds, the bird hopped right back, even chirping angrily in his direction a few times.

Song Yu froze.

Qi Siyang raised an eyebrow slightly, watching his junior brother brush it away once more. The bird was so angry its feathers puffed up completely, yet it still stubbornly hopped back onto Song Yu's hand.

"Haha, it really likes you."

Bai Linlin was instantly frozen in embarrassment.

"."

It had puffed up its feathers for ages, only to look incredibly pathetic.

But perhaps those words actually had an effect. Song Yu didn't say anything more after that and saw the two guests out.

Bai Linlin stood on the young man's shoulder, leisurely preening his feathers. Victory in this battle!

The night was as still as water. The wall lamp by the kitchen island was turned on, casting a warm, atmospheric yellow glow.

It was just that the bird happened to stand right behind the light, casting a massive shadow on the wall that shifted with every movement, looking highly "majestic."

"Chirp, chirp?"

Song Yu, lost in thought, lowered his head to send a text message, notifying the housekeeper auntie that she didn't need to come over tonight.

He went to the kitchen. The little bird on his shoulder actually had some weight to it, feeling quite solid. Occasionally, he could feel it tilting its head, sizing him up.

It was a very subtle feeling.

Song Yu had lived alone for a very long time. His private space usually contained only himself, but now there was... a bird.

And it seemed to like him?

Song Yu's face was pale, and his eyes were pitch-black like thick ink. He suffered from mild somatization symptoms.

But now, for some unknown reason, he didn't take his medicine immediately.

Instead, he walked over to the cabinet, took out a small dish, and poured some bird food.

This was the only thing he knew how to do...

Did this count as raising it?

No.

Song Yu stared blankly at the items on the counter. Everything was a mess, and chaotic fragments of information clashed in his mind.

[Xiao Song, your mother is pregnant again. Could you please not call her for the next few days?]

[You know it's not very convenient.]

...

[Song Yu, I don't have time to look after you. It's not like I gave birth to you. Go find your mother.]

[Who's calling? Yangyang has been clamoring to find you today.]

[Aw, baby, you're out of school? Let Daddy hug you.]

These voices, male and female, sometimes harsh and sometimes gentle, were like masked impostors, constantly devouring his sanity.

"Chirp, chirp?"

Song Yu startled, his fingers freezing cold. He was instantly pulled out of his hallucinations. A slight itch tickled his cheek, and he turned his head to look.

The bird's head was nudging him.

It was fluffy and soft.

Song Yu raised his hand slightly. The little bird's head was perfectly round. It peered at him for a moment longer before extending its legs and stepping firmly onto the "human perch."

The bird food in the dish was fresh, consisting of tiny pellets. The extrusion process was excellent, with almost no crushed crumbs.

Bai Linlin was placed onto the counter. He fell into a brief silence. *Do I really have to eat this?*

He looked up at the youth.

As usual, Song Yu showed no major expression. However, at this distance, the marks on his wrist bone were particularly clear, looking like cuts made by a utility knife...

Bai Linlin was still a bit worried.

The bird cannot leave.

The bird has a sense of social responsibility.

He thought about it and decided that taking a few perfunctory bites would be fine. So, he lowered his head and pecked at a pellet.

*Smack, smack.*

Bai Linlin felt it tasted a bit like oatmeal, but with a hint of fresh grass. It was actually quite addictive.

He took another bite.

Song Yu looked down, seemingly letting out a sigh of relief, but then his brow furrowed slightly. He always felt like he had forgotten something.

But it was already very late.

He planned to make do with a few slices of bread, so he walked over to the refrigerator, reached out, and pulled the door open.

He froze.

Because the inside could only be described as "an absolute disaster." All the plastic wrap had been punctured and torn to shreds. It wasn't just the braised meat in the bowl; there were also carrots and baby napa cabbage with bite marks, and even the caps of ordinary beverage bottles had neat little gashes pecked into them.

"..."

chunks.chineseText:
第5章

卧室。

白粼粼被握着，鸟腿垂着，偶尔试图探头去看宋郁的手机屏幕，但还是看不太清。

好像是聊天软件。

师弟：[胡萝卜和青菜？那还好吧，它居然能撬开……]

宋郁坐在书桌的椅子上，指缝里还捻着那根被鸟充当装饰物的“纸条”，面色仍然有些困惑。

他的空闲时间消失了。

全部被一个小动物给占据了，但他本人其实并不能完全适应。

放生……不现实。

宋郁：[它可能吃了卤肉。]

对面迅速回复：

师弟：[不可能，鹦鹉顶多是叨两口玩一玩，不会吃的，那香辛料很多。]

师弟：[没什么事，你把冰箱门关紧就可以了。]

宋郁没有话要说了，修长的手指传来点湿润的感觉，少年抬眸一看，鸟正在专心致志地叨。

白粼粼：“……”

鸟松开了，黑松石一般的鸟眼看了过来。

但或许是因为眼睛是在两侧，白粼粼习惯于歪头观察宋郁。

这个姿势，显得很睿智。

“你是怎么打开的呢……”

宋郁有些出神地道，他换了家居服，锁骨若隐若现的，少年的青春气息尽显无遗，那根纸条在手指内侧卷了下。

大约一个小时后。

鸟被赶出了卧室。

宋郁其实是买了个笼子的，空间很大，但白粼粼压根不进，他没有什么经验，觉得可能是小鸟觉得闭塞。

那索性外面的空间都是它的。

别墅里的窗户全部封好了，没有飞出去的可能性。

白粼粼站在卧室门口外头，一阵沉默，觉得不行，在地板上蹦跶了两下。

问题一：别墅里好像只有宋郁一个人，那如果自己要做一些事，必须要依靠“人”。

问题二：“人”把“鸟”关出去了。

“……”

其实这是有些戏剧化的，一般宠物夜里是有笼养的，但有的主人为了确保自己爱宠的自由，选择给自己买了笼子，然后周遭趴着无数个猫猫和狗狗。

白粼粼压根不想去那个豪华鸟笼，他只想打游戏，很想，这是社畜下班之后的唯一爱好了。

电子竞技，谁与争锋！

于是乎，鸟站在门口，深沉地望着门把手，扑棱翅膀飞了上去。

开始往下“墩墩”。

具体表现在，一只圆滚滚的“小鸡”在上下用力踩门把手。

与此同时，宋郁在洗澡，温热的水流划过高挺的鼻梁，黑色的瞳仁里面没有什么光彩，只是看着暗沉沉的。

不过就在抬手拿毛巾擦头发的时候，听到了熟悉的细细簌簌的动静。

浴室门是磨砂制的，门口有一坨小小的身影，大摇大摆地叨了几下门。

鸟头一探一探的，似乎是很好奇。

宋郁蹙了蹙眉，索性直接拉开门了，浴室里的雾气也随之四处逃窜。

白粼粼被这阵开门的风给带的有些不稳，有一滴水落下，翅膀给弄湿了。

欸，洗澡。

他也想洗。

宋郁衣着完整，发梢沾水，只是附身蹲下，面无表情地伸过去了手。

鸟很满意地站上去了。

宋郁也不知道自己怎么了，或许是白天事情太多，他也有些烦躁，开始自动合理化。

鸟可能就是比较聪明的，冰箱门都可以打开，一个门有什么所谓。

这很正常。

别的鸟估计也会。

对，是这样。

宋郁抬手带着鸟回到了书桌那里，伸手靠着桌面，沉甸甸的小鸟挪动了下，他甚至能感受到爪子包裹手指的感觉，大约挪了几下位置。

下来了。

白粼粼伸展了下翅膀，估计是被打湿了点，整个鸟蓬松了起来。

像个毛球。

宋郁垂眸看了一眼，再度脑海成像：

[毛绒钥匙扣]

现在已经晚上八点半了，四月份的天气不算太热，窗户外面的树叶晃来晃去的，倒是十分静谧。

白粼粼在书桌上站着，看着宋郁抬手吃药，还注意到了对方撇过来的目光，淡淡的。

其实是有点：你在看我？

白粼粼可是光明正大地看的，现在他可是鸟了，切，衣服都不用穿。

爽得很。

宋郁果然没有再赶他，只是拉开椅子，开了电脑。

白粼粼：！！

鸟腿此刻走得很快，立马飞到了宋郁的肩头，准备去看开机密码。

[20070506]

白粼粼一下子就记住了，心里美滋滋，他还复习了下上次的支付密码：

[******]

好好好。

宋郁其实在输完密码就没有在动作，因为肩头站着只小鸟，他不太能分辨这是否是那位师弟说的“喜欢”。

但，不排斥。

爪子的存在感其实很强，稍微挪动一下，他就能想象到圆滚滚的“甜筒”在调整站姿。

比如现在。

宋郁面无表情，只有握着鼠标的手指微微动了下。

鸟的确在调整姿势，还时不时地张开翅膀，似乎是在梳理打湿的羽毛。

又蓬了一个度。

宋郁不知道自己在干什么。

“啾啾啾啾？”

白粼粼歪头看了过去，爪子往里面踩了踩，找了个合适位置窝好了，很是不解。

[玩游戏呀。]

宋郁回了下神，随便打开了个MOBA游戏，不过在等待匹配的时候，他察觉到肩头的一些动作。

爪子似乎往前伸了。

“……”

他在分心，甚至角色差点被一个蹲草的敌人杀了，不过好在丝血跑了。

“啾啾！”

宋郁唇角是平直的，眼皮垂着，一边操作，一边走神。

鸟腿往前一伸，它直接坐下了。

毛绒绒的。

宋郁操作的手指都停了。

不出所料，屏幕黑了。

白粼粼震惊，这在干什么，这在干什么？

死了，兄弟你怎么死了？

“啾啾啾啾啾啾！”

宋郁感觉肩头热热的，同时，也吵吵的，或许是吃了药的缘故，夜里竟然没有那么难熬。

打游戏到了十一点。

把把都是胜方mvp，宋郁面色很平静，输赢不重要，只是排解时间而已。

他本来是要起身的，但是肩头的小鸟似乎睡着了，一动不动。

宋郁坐在椅子上，没有再动过。

深夜了。

他的视线落在了桌面的那本书上，或许是心念一动，拿了过来，动作很轻。

封皮被啃出来一个条。

宋郁垂眸随便看了看教辅，都是再基础不过的知识，没什么好看的。

也就在这时，肩头一轻。

鸟迷迷瞪瞪地栽了下来，但本能地扑棱翅膀和伸爪子，半道把“人”的睡衣扣子给弄开了，在对方的锁骨上划出了一道痕迹。

宋郁抬手接住了。

白粼粼困死了，最后一个朦胧的记忆是被放进了一个四四方方的纸巾盒里。

-

四月天气，南市风景如画。

宋郁一大早就在打电话，掌心躺着一只两脚朝天、一动不动的鸟，宛若是……死了。

手机那边传来安慰的声音。

齐思扬：“应该不会……身体是热的吗？”

宋郁垂眸看着鸟，指腹碰了下那滑滑的肉色短喙，随即又滑到鸟头那里，摸了下。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 5

Bedroom.

Bai Linlin was being held, his little legs dangling. Occasionally, he tried to crane his neck to look at Song Yu's phone screen, but he still couldn't see it clearly.

It seemed to be a chat app.

Junior Brother: [Carrots and green vegetables? That's not too bad. I can't believe it actually managed to pry them open...]

Song Yu sat in his desk chair, still twirling the "paper strip" that the bird had used as an ornament between his fingers. His face still carried a hint of confusion.

His free time had vanished.

It was entirely occupied by a small animal, but he himself couldn't fully adapt to it.

Releasing it back into the wild... was unrealistic.

Song Yu: [It might have eaten the braised meat.]

The other side replied instantly:

Junior Brother: [Impossible. At most, a parrot would peck at it a couple of times for fun. It wouldn't eat it; there are too many spices in there.]

Junior Brother: [It's fine. Just make sure you shut the fridge door tightly.]

Song Yu had nothing left to say. A slight damp sensation came from his slender fingers. The youth looked up and saw the bird diligently pecking at them.

Bai Linlin: "..."

The bird let go, its dark turquoise-like eyes looking over.

But perhaps because its eyes were on the sides of its head, Bai Linlin was used to tilting his head to observe Song Yu.

This posture made him look highly intelligent.

"How did you open it..."

Song Yu murmured, somewhat dazed. He had changed into loungewear, his collarbones faintly visible, fully showcasing the youth's youthful aura. The paper strip curled slightly against the inside of his fingers.

About an hour later.

The bird was kicked out of the bedroom.

Song Yu had actually bought a cage, and a very spacious one at that, but Bai Linlin refused to go inside. Lacking experience, Song Yu figured the little bird might find it too claustrophobic.

So, he simply let it have the run of the space outside.

All the windows in the villa were sealed, so there was no possibility of it flying out.

Bai Linlin stood outside the bedroom door in silence. Feeling that this wouldn't do, he hopped twice on the floor.

Problem one: Song Yu seemed to be the only person in the villa. If he wanted to do anything, he had to rely on a "human."

Problem two: The "human" had locked the "bird" out.

"..."

Actually, this was somewhat comical. Normally, pets were caged at night, but some owners, to ensure their beloved pets' freedom, chose to buy a cage for themselves while countless cats and dogs lounged around them.

Bai Linlin didn't want to go to that luxurious birdcage at all. He just wanted to play video games—badly. This was a corporate slave's sole hobby after getting off work.

Esports! Who dares challenge me!

And so, the bird stood at the door, staring solemnly at the doorknob, before flapping his wings and flying up to it.

He began to "stomp" downward.

Specifically, a plump little "chicken" was stomping hard up and down on the doorknob.

Meanwhile, Song Yu was taking a shower. Warm water flowed over his high nose bridge. His black pupils lacked luster, looking dark and gloomy.

But just as he reached for a towel to dry his hair, he heard a familiar rustling sound.

The bathroom door was made of frosted glass. A small, round silhouette stood at the door, swaggering over to peck at it a few times.

The bird's head bobbed up and down, seemingly very curious.

Song Yu furrowed his brow and simply pulled the door open, letting the steam from the bathroom billow out.

Bai Linlin was thrown slightly off balance by the draft from the opening door. A drop of water fell, wetting his wing.

*Oh, a shower.*

*He wanted to take one too.*

Song Yu was fully dressed, the tips of his hair dripping with water. He simply bent down, squatted, and extended his hand expressionlessly.

The bird stepped onto it with great satisfaction.

Song Yu didn't know what was wrong with him. Perhaps because too many things had happened during the day, he was also somewhat irritable, so he began to automatically rationalize it.

*The bird is probably just on the smarter side. If it can open a fridge door, what's a regular door?*

*This is normal.*

*Other birds can probably do it too.*

*Yes, that's it.*

Song Yu raised his hand to bring the bird back to the desk. He rested his hand near the desktop. The heavy little bird shifted around. He could even feel its claws wrapping around his fingers as it adjusted its position a few times.

It stepped down.

Bai Linlin stretched his wings. Probably because they were slightly damp, the entire bird puffed up.

Like a fluffball.

Song Yu glanced down, and an image formed in his mind once more:

[Plush keychain]

It was already 8:30 PM. The April weather wasn't too hot. Outside the window, the leaves swayed gently, making the night exceptionally quiet.

Bai Linlin stood on the desk, watching Song Yu take his medicine. He also noticed the youth's sideways glance, which was quite faint.

It was almost like: *Are you looking at me?*

Bai Linlin was looking at him completely out in the open. He was a bird now anyway—psh, he didn't even have to wear clothes.

It was incredibly liberating.

Sure enough, Song Yu didn't chase him away again. He simply pulled out his chair and turned on the computer.

Bai Linlin: !!

His bird legs moved rapidly now. He immediately flew onto Song Yu's shoulder, preparing to peek at the startup password.

[20070506]

Bai Linlin memorized it instantly, feeling delighted. He even reviewed the payment password from last time:

[******]

*Good, good, good.*

Song Yu actually didn't make another move after entering the password. Because a little bird was perched on his shoulder, he couldn't quite tell if this was the "liking" his junior brother had mentioned.

But he didn't reject it.

The presence of the claws was actually very strong. With just a slight shift, he could picture the plump "ice cream cone" adjusting its stance.

Like right now.

Song Yu remained expressionless, only the finger holding the mouse twitching slightly.

The bird was indeed adjusting its posture, occasionally spreading its wings as if preening its damp feathers.

It puffed up another level.

Song Yu didn't know what he was doing.

"Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp?"

Bai Linlin tilted his head to look at him, stepping inward to find a comfortable spot to nestle down, looking highly puzzled.

*Play the game.*

Song Yu snapped out of it and casually opened a MOBA game. However, while waiting for matchmaking, he noticed some movement on his shoulder.

The claws seemed to stretch forward.

"..."

He was distracted, and his character was almost killed by an enemy hiding in the brush. Fortunately, he managed to escape with a sliver of health.

"Chirp, chirp!"

Song Yu's lips were in a flat line, his eyelids drooping. He was playing while letting his mind wander.

The bird extended its legs forward and sat down directly.

It was so fluffy.

Song Yu's fingers on the controls completely stopped.

Unsurprisingly, the screen went black.

Bai Linlin was shocked. *What are you doing? What are you doing?*

*You're dead! Brother, how did you die?*

"Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!"

Song Yu felt a warmth on his shoulder, and at the same time, it was quite noisy. Perhaps because he had taken his medicine, the night didn't seem so unbearable.

He played games until eleven o'clock.

He was the winning MVP in every single match. Song Yu's face was very calm; winning or losing didn't matter, it was just a way to pass the time.

He was originally going to stand up, but the little bird on his shoulder seemed to have fallen asleep, completely motionless.

Song Yu sat in the chair and didn't move again.

It was late at night.

His gaze fell upon the book on the desk. On a sudden whim, he reached over and picked it up, his movements very gentle.

A strip had been chewed out of the cover.

Song Yu looked down and casually flipped through the study guide. It was all basic knowledge, nothing interesting to look at.

Just then, his shoulder lightened.

The bird tumbled down in a daze, but instinctively flapped its wings and extended its claws. Midway, it snagged and undid the "human's" pajama button, scratching a mark across his collarbone.

Song Yu reached out and caught it.

Bai Linlin was dead tired. His last hazy memory was being placed into a square tissue box.

-

In the April weather, Nan City was as picturesque as a painting.

Song Yu was on the phone early in the morning. In his palm lay a bird with its feet pointing straight up in the air, completely motionless, as if... it were dead.

A comforting voice came from the other end of the phone.

Qi Siyang: "Probably not... Is its body warm?"

Song Yu looked down at the bird. His fingertip touched its smooth, flesh-colored short beak, then slid up to the bird's head, giving it a gentle stroke.

chunks.chineseText:
“热的。”他同电话里的人说道。

对面的人似乎是沉默了一会，最后给出了比较专业的解释：

“那应该就是在睡觉，但是说实话，和尚鹦鹉这个品种，仰躺睡姿并不常见，除非从小养到大……”

“而且它应该很警觉才是，你都把它拿出来了，那照理说该醒了，啧……”

齐思扬觉得离谱，但最后发现一句也解释不了，什么神鸟？

宋郁垂眸等了一会，直到指腹传来一阵刺痛，小鸟叨了他一口。

“它醒了。”

电话就此中断。

齐思扬在工位上坐着，整个人都有些反应不过来，他回顾了下本科所学的知识，仍然不是很懂宋郁所口述的现象。

摇都摇不醒？

鹦鹉？

他觉得还是很奇怪，不过顺道同自己老师发了个邮件，说了下近期的项目进度以及宋郁的……近况。

与此同时。

白粼粼整个鸟都很困，站在宋郁的肩头张了张喙，肉色的小舌头往外伸了伸，然后收回，翅膀也合了合。

像是打哈欠。

宋郁在洗漱，神色淡淡的，但是抬眼看镜子的时候，还是把目光偏移了下。

鸟羽毛蓬松，站得稳稳当当。

鸟眼都还眯着。

宋郁尽管没什么反应，但还是避开了弯腰的动作，眼皮微微垂着，能感受到隔着布料的爪子挪动。

白粼粼执意不走路，一路都在人身上小憩，直到他被一把握了起来，挪到了餐桌上，上面放着一盘鸟粮。

宋郁就站在旁边，垂眸看着他。

有些时候仿佛不需要说话。

鸟仰头。

人抬手把盘子挪了过去。

鸟歪了下头，觉得还是敷衍一下，点了点头，示意自己知道了。

宋郁再度怔住了，不过或许是昨日已经有了经验，没在因为这件事去联系齐思扬。

说不定这个品种的小鸟都是这么聪慧的。

很正常，会点头怎么了？

理所应当。

白粼粼站上了盘子的边边，抬头看了下宋郁，为了符合鸟设，叨了几口鸟粮。

对方果然放心了许多，背着书包就走了。

白粼粼想了想，扑棱翅膀下地，很是兢兢业业地送了送人。

等到玄关门关上的时候。

一秒，两秒。

鸟鬼鬼祟祟，飞到了一楼窗户那里，确保对方真的走了之后。

“啾啾啾啾啾！！！”

[耶耶耶耶耶耶。]

白粼粼从善如流地飞到厨房，开始一段美食寻觅，尾羽微微上翘，圆滚滚的身子被冰箱夹住了也浑然不觉。

不知道过了多久，门口那里有密码输入的声音，钟点工阿姨提着新鲜的蔬菜就上门了。

路上还有几名健身的邻居打招呼。

“张姨又过来了啊？”

“啊是。”

“也是辛苦你了，那孩子也是可怜……”

作者有话说：

是的，每个人都将知道宋郁的支付密码
chunks.englishText:
"It's warm," he said to the person on the phone.

The person on the other end seemed to fall silent for a moment before finally offering a more professional explanation:

"Then it should just be sleeping. But to be honest, for Quaker parrots, sleeping on their backs isn't very common unless they've been raised like that since they were chicks..."

"And it should be very alert. You've already picked it up, so logically speaking, it should have woken up. Tsk..."

Qi Siyang found it absurd, but in the end, he realized he couldn't explain a single thing. What kind of divine bird was this?

Song Yu looked down and waited for a moment, until a sharp pain pricked his fingertip. The little bird had pecked him.

"It's awake."

The call was disconnected.

Qi Siyang sat at his workstation, unable to fully process things. He reviewed the knowledge he had learned during his undergraduate studies, but he still couldn't quite understand the phenomenon Song Yu had described.

*You can't even shake it awake?*

*A parrot?*

He still found it very strange, but he sent an email to his advisor anyway, reporting on the recent project progress and Song Yu's... recent situation.

Meanwhile.

Bai Linlin was incredibly sleepy. Standing on Song Yu's shoulder, he opened his beak, stuck out his tiny, flesh-colored tongue, retracted it, and folded his wings.

It looked like a yawn.

Song Yu was washing up, his expression indifferent. But when he looked up at the mirror, his gaze shifted slightly.

The bird's feathers were fluffy, and it stood perfectly steady.

Its bird eyes were still squinted shut.

Although Song Yu showed no reaction, he still avoided bending over. With his eyelids slightly lowered, he could feel the claws shifting through the fabric of his clothes.

Bai Linlin adamantly refused to walk, dozing on the human the entire way until he was scooped up in a hand and moved to the dining table, where a dish of bird food was placed.

Song Yu stood right beside him, looking down at him.

Sometimes, words seemed unnecessary.

The bird looked up.

The human reached out and pushed the dish closer.

The bird tilted its head. Deciding to put on a perfunctory show, it nodded its head to indicate it understood.

Song Yu froze once more. However, perhaps because he had gained some experience yesterday, he didn't contact Qi Siyang over this.

*Maybe little birds of this breed are just this intelligent.*

*It's normal. What's so strange about a bird nodding?*

*It's only natural.*

Bai Linlin stepped onto the rim of the dish and looked up at Song Yu. To stay in character as a bird, he pecked at the bird food a few times.

Sure enough, the other party looked much more reassured. He slung his backpack over his shoulder and left.

Bai Linlin thought about it, flapped his wings down to the floor, and very diligently saw him off.

Once the front door clicked shut.

One second, two seconds.

The bird acted stealthily, flying over to the first-floor window. After ensuring the other party had truly left:

"Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!!!"

*[Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah!]*

Bai Linlin naturally flew to the kitchen to begin a quest for delicious food. His tail feathers curled upward slightly, and he didn't even notice when his plump body got wedged in the fridge door.

After an unknown amount of time, the sound of a passcode being entered came from the entrance. The hourly housekeeper auntie arrived, carrying fresh vegetables.

On her way, several neighbors who were working out greeted her.

"Auntie Zhang, you're here again?"

"Ah, yes."

"It's hard on you too. That child is really quite pitiful..."

***

**Author's Note:**

Yes, everyone is going to find out Song Yu's payment password.

chunks.chineseText:
第6章

阿姨进门之后就把买来的新鲜蔬菜放到了桌上，准备去给做几个三明治，顺带也去预热了烤箱。

厨房里一阵阵的香气。

不过就在这时，阿姨口袋里的手机嗡嗡震动了起来，对面似乎是个中年男人。

“是，先生，我知道。”

“小宋也就上次去见他母亲了，最近没有再去过。”

“好，好，我知道了。”

白粼粼站在吊灯上面，鸟头往下垂着，非常严谨地观察新的“人”。

阿姨挂了电话后就叹了口气，但还是很利索地忙活了起来，但就在打开冰箱的时候，微微怔了下。

里面乱糟糟的，蔬菜胡萝卜也有一些坑坑洼洼的印记。

白粼粼活动了下鸟腿，短喙上还有点酸奶的痕迹，不过很快被咂巴干净了。

继续观察。

阿姨还没有进行下一步动作，又一个电话过来了，这次对面是宋郁。

“张姨，我给您发过消息了，您不用过来给我做饭。”

电话那边的声音很是冷淡，但还是保持了礼貌与客气。

但阿姨也有些为难，只是解释道，“我、我看到了，但是，先生那边……不好交代。”

别墅的智能门锁有密钥，宋父即使在国外，也可以授权管理。

那边沉默了一会。

宋郁几乎有些烦躁，“那我回来。”

白粼粼只能听出来个大概，他站在吊灯上，需要往下探探鸟头。

大抵是阿姨一直在道歉，说做完饭就会离开，同时也在劝说：

“小宋好好上课，是我的错，这、这我家里实在是缺钱，这份工作我暂时没办法不做，你请假的话，校方那里肯定要联系先生的，还是不要……”

白粼粼听着就窒息。

什么乱七八糟的。

后面不知道具体说了什么，但很快阿姨语气就变了，开始四处张望。

“是吗？哎呀，我没见到它呀。”

妇人更内疚了，在厨房里走来走去，甚至开始准备的去客厅那里找。

白粼粼本来是低头看着的，为了跟随目标移动，鸟头转得有点费劲，只能调整一下爪子，但这个古董吊灯实在是叮叮咣咣的。

刚一挪动，那阿姨就愣愣地抬头看了过来：

“小宋，找到了。”

十分钟后——

宋郁的手机屏幕里出现了一个鸟头，圆滚滚的，似乎是站在餐桌上，短喙张了张，似乎是打了哈欠。

这还是阿姨费了好些功夫哄下来的，一开始是用鸟粮，但压根不管用，最后是用得带回来的熟切火腿。

但白粼粼一口没有叨到，一个庞大的手机摄像头就对了过来。

对面的阿姨很是热络地对准小鸟，非常实心实意地夸赞：

“欸，这长得，真好看真好看。”

“小鸟小鸟，看镜头。”

“你主人在看你噢。”

白粼粼一时半会有点鸟脸泛红，这怎么和哄小孩一样？

阿姨还特地把摄像头给反转了下，用手当成小支架，给鸟去看屏幕里的主人。

宋郁倚靠在栏杆上，周遭没有人，好像是天台，额发有些微微吹起，眉眼在日光下显得尤为出众。

“……”

白粼粼不知道说什么，思来想去，对着人“啾啾”了几声。

手机摄像是有畸变的，鸟头圆滚滚占据了整个屏幕，短喙一张一合的，像是贴到“人”的脸上一样。

宋郁面无表情，但截了图。

这个视频通话，其实还是阿姨说的话比较多。

“取名字了吗？小宋。”

“还没有。”

“那要取个名字的，小动物也是家里的一份子，哎呀哎呀，真好。”

阿姨其实是很欣慰的，这孩子她也照顾半年了，对宋家的事也是知道一二的，了解内情之后很难不会心疼。

小鸟好，小鸟可以陪陪小宋。

白粼粼在餐桌上站着板板正正的，一开始有点无聊，不过后来看着屏幕里的宋郁，不知道怎么了，叨了一口。

“……”

少年垂眸看着，眉眼平和。

白粼粼歪了歪鸟头，又叨了一口。

“……”

最后还是上课铃响了结束了这场“无聊”的互动，阿姨在准备拿起来手机在说几句的时候，鸟往前走了走，探头探脑的。

“小宋中午吃什么？阿姨提前做好。”

“好好，你放心，我没有开门窗，小鸟很安全的。”

……

白粼粼瞅准时机，扑棱翅膀飞了过去，叨了下手机屏幕。

正好按到挂断键上。

阿姨又是一阵惊叹，连连夸了鸟好多句，一时半会甚至做饭都给忘了。

白粼粼非常矜持地又展示了自己的才艺，在桌子上飞了一圈，完美落地。

“小鸟，你好会飞呀！”

“来来来，阿姨给你拍照，发给我们小宋。”

白粼粼的虚荣心得到了极大的膨胀，不当人之后，世界都美好了起来。

-

大约三十分钟后。

阿姨认真查阅手机，给鸟切了一个指甲盖大的苹果肉，顺带把刚刚拍的图片都传给了宋郁。

她是不担心那孩子的学习的。

虽然生病了，但好像年年都是第一。

适当放松下也是好的。

白粼粼叼起来苹果认真地炫了，探头探脑的，看着厨房灶台上熬着的玉米排骨汤，非常心动。

但他现在肯定不能吃……

鸟自己在家也有些无聊，又吃了一小块苹果，想了想，飞到了二楼去。

白粼粼熟门熟路地站在门把手上，带着自己的身体“墩了墩”，很轻松就打开了。

随后的流程就比较紧张刺激了。

白粼粼先是叨开开机键，然后认真站在电脑屏幕前等待开机，随后正儿八经地输入密码。

开始战斗！

键盘其实是有些大的，鸟腿几乎要分叉，时不时还对用喙来叨一口。

最后打出来0-12-0的战绩。

“……”

白粼粼当然不服输，他好说歹说也是个学计算机出身的，电脑按键的问题而已，大约捯饬了有半个小时。

又美美开了一局。

不过这次自己不是人机操作了，队友却变人机了，技能乱放，上去送死，完了最后开麦一直说：

[欸，这里有活人吗？]

白粼粼怒了，翅膀一挥，开启麦克风。

[啾啾啾啾啾啾啾啾啾！！]

[啾啾啾啾！]

队友懵了，一直在左下角聊天框里问：

[哪里来的鸟？]

[不是哥们，用鸟骂人？]

[你可玩的太脏了。]

白粼粼生气了，在死了的时候，一个字一个敲：

[我家鸟来打，都比你玩的好。]

对面彻底破防了。

最后打完这局游戏已经中午了，二楼走廊里传来阿姨的声音。

“小鸟在哪里呀？”

白粼粼只好关了游戏，利索地踩了关机键，然后愤愤不平地用喙推了推鼠标。

人机！

简直是人机！

不过能打游戏还是幸福的，他扑棱翅膀飞到了门口，果然看见了阿姨，不过对方似乎没有要进来的意思，只是在等着。

妇人很是温和地道：“哎呀，我就猜你在里面呀，我给小鸟勾了个围兜。”

“来来来。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 6

Upon entering, the auntie placed the fresh vegetables she had bought onto the table. She prepared to make a few sandwiches and preheated the oven while she was at it.

Whiffs of mouthwatering aroma soon wafted from the kitchen.

Just then, the phone in her pocket buzzed. The voice on the other end sounded like a middle-aged man.

"Yes, sir. I understand."

"Young Song only went to see his mother that one time. He hasn't gone back recently."

"Alright, alright. Understood."

Perched atop the chandelier, Bai Linlin lowered his feathery head, observing this new "human" with utmost solemnity.

Auntie Zhang let out a sigh after hanging up, but she quickly busied herself again with deft movements. However, when she opened the refrigerator, she froze for a moment.

The inside was a chaotic mess. The vegetables and carrots bore small, pitted peck marks.

Bai Linlin stretched his tiny bird legs. A bit of leftover yogurt still clung to his short beak, but he quickly licked it clean with a smack of his lips.

He resumed his observation.

Before Auntie Zhang could make her next move, another call came through. This time, it was Song Yu.

"Auntie Zhang, I sent you a message earlier. You don’t need to come over to cook for me."

The voice over the line was chilly, yet it maintained a polite and courteous distance.

Auntie Zhang felt caught in a bind and explained hesitantly, "I—I saw it, but... your father's side... it's hard for me to report back to him."

The villa's smart lock had digital access keys. Even while overseas, Mr. Song could authorize and monitor access.

Silence fell on the other end for a moment.

Song Yu sounded borderlined irritated. "Fine. I'm coming back."

Bai Linlin could only catch the gist of it. Perched on the chandelier, he had to crane his little head downward.

Auntie Zhang was essentially apologizing non-stop, promising she would leave as soon as she finished cooking while trying to persuade him:

"Young Song, focus on your classes. It's my fault... My family is really short on money right now, so I really can't afford to quit this job. If you ask for leave, the school will definitely contact your father, so please don't..."

Bai Linlin felt suffocated just listening to this melodrama. What a convoluted mess.

He couldn't hear what was said next, but Auntie Zhang's tone soon shifted, and she began looking around anxiously.

"Is that so? Oh dear, I haven't seen it!"

Overwhelmed with guilt, the woman paced back and forth in the kitchen before turning toward the living room to search.

Bai Linlin had been staring down at her. To track her movement, he strained his neck a little too far, so he adjusted his claws on the vintage antique chandelier. The old fixture clinked and clattered instantly.

The second he shifted, Auntie Zhang looked up in shock.

"Young Song, I found it!"

***

Ten minutes later—

A round, chubby bird head appeared on Song Yu's phone screen. Standing on the dining table, the bird opened its short beak wide and gave a tiny yawn.

Auntie Zhang had spent quite a bit of effort coaxing him down. She had tried bird seed first, which failed utterly, before finally succeeding with some sliced cooked ham she brought along.

Before Bai Linlin could even steal a bite, a massive phone camera lens was thrust right into his face.

Auntie Zhang enthusiastically pointed the camera at the little bird, complimenting him from the bottom of her heart.

"Aww, look at you! What a handsome little guy!"

"Little bird, look at the camera!"

"Your master is watching you!"

Bai Linlin felt his bird face flush red. Why was she treating him like a toddler?

Auntie Zhang flipped the camera view and propped the phone up with her hands like a makeshift stand so the bird could see its master on the screen.

Song Yu was leaning against a railing. There was no one around him—it looked like a rooftop. His bangs fluttered gently in the breeze, his sharp, handsome features looking exceptionally striking under the sunlight.

"..."

Bai Linlin had no idea what to say. After mulling it over, he let out a few soft chirps at the screen.

The phone camera's lens distortion made his round bird head fill the entire display. As his short beak opened and closed, it looked almost as if he were pressing his face directly against the youth's cheek.

Song Yu remained expressionless, but he silently snapped a screenshot.

Auntie Zhang did most of the talking during the video call.

"Have you named it yet, Young Song?"

"Not yet."

"You definitely should give it a name! A pet is part of the family too. Oh my, how wonderful."

Auntie Zhang genuinely felt relieved. She had taken care of the boy for half a year now and knew a thing or two about the Song family affairs. Knowing the inside story, it was impossible not to feel heartbroken for him. Having a little bird was wonderful; it could keep Young Song company.

Bai Linlin stood perfectly upright on the dining table. At first, he found it a bit boring, but as he stared at Song Yu on the screen, an inexplicable urge took over, and he pecked at the image.

"..."

The youth lowered his gaze, his expression placid.

"..."

Bai Linlin tilted his head, giving another peck.

"..."

Ultimately, the bell signaling the start of class put an end to this "boring" interaction. As Auntie Zhang picked up the phone to say a few more words, the bird waddled forward, craning its head curiously.

"What would you like for lunch, Young Song? Auntie will prepare it ahead of time."

"Alright, don't worry. I haven't opened any doors or windows. The little bird is completely safe."

...

Bai Linlin seized the moment, flapped his wings, and swooped over to peck directly at the screen.

His beak hit the red end-call button square on target.

Auntie Zhang gasped in awe once more, heaping praise upon praise on the little bird, momentarily forgetting all about cooking.

Bai Linlin magnanimously put his talents on display again, taking a smooth lap around the table before executing a flawless landing.

"Little bird, you fly so well!"

"Come, come, Auntie will take a picture of you and send it to our Young Song."

Bai Linlin's vanity swelled to immense proportions. Life truly became so much better once he stopped being human.

-

About thirty minutes later.

Auntie Zhang carefully checked her phone and sliced a piece of apple flesh about the size of a fingernail for the bird, sending all the photos she had just taken over to Song Yu.

She was never worried about the boy's studies. Although he was sick, he still placed first every year. It was good for him to relax a bit.

Bai Linlin snatched up the apple piece and devoured it enthusiastically. Wandering around with his head poking everywhere, he cast a longing glance at the corn and pork rib soup simmering on the kitchen stove.

Sadly, he definitely couldn't eat that right now...

Feeling a bit bored being home alone with Auntie busy, he ate another tiny piece of apple, pondered for a moment, and flew up to the second floor.

Bai Linlin expertly landed on the door handle, bouncing his body up and down a couple of times. The door popped open with ease.

What followed was a thrilling, edge-of-your-seat sequence.

Bai Linlin pecked the power button on the computer, then stood solemnly in front of the monitor waiting for it to boot up. Next, he entered the password with practiced accuracy.

Time to battle!

The keyboard was honestly a bit too big for him. His tiny bird legs had to stretch to near-splits, and he occasionally had to use his beak to hit keys.

His final KDA score: 0-12-0.

"..."

Bai Linlin refused to accept defeat. He was a Computer Science major, for goodness' sake! It was merely a mechanical issue with the physical keys. After tinkering and practicing for about half an hour, he joyfully queued up for another match.

This time, he wasn't playing like a bot anymore—but his teammates had turned into absolute bots! They randomly cast skills, threw themselves into enemy fire to feed, and to top it off, one teammate turned on their mic and droned on:

[Hey, is anyone actually alive in this lobby?]

Bai Linlin was furious! With a sweep of his wing, he unmuted the microphone.

"CHIRP CHIRP CHIRP CHIRP CHIRP CHIRP!!"

"CHIRP CHIRP CHIRP CHIRP!"

The teammate was completely bewildered, frantically typing in the lower-left chat box:

[Where is that bird coming from?]

[Bro, are you using a bird to flame me?]

[Damn, that's playing dirty.]

Enraged, Bai Linlin waited until he died in-game, then painstakingly pecked out letter by letter:

[Even if my family's bird played, it'd play better than you.]

The teammate suffered a total mental breakdown.

By the time the match ended, it was already noon. Auntie Zhang's voice echoed from the hallway outside the second floor.

"Where is the little bird?"

Bai Linlin had no choice but to close the game. He nimbly stomped the power key to shut down, then angrily shoved the mouse aside with his beak.

NPCs! Absolute bot teammates!

Still, being able to play video games was pure bliss. He flapped his wings and flew to the doorway. Sure enough, Auntie Zhang was waiting outside, though she didn't seem to have any intention of barging in.

The woman said warmly, "Oh my, I guessed you were in here! I crocheted a little bib for you!"

"Come here, little bird, come here!"

chunks.chineseText:
宋郁中午回来的时候，看到的就是带着黄色围兜的小鸟，在餐桌那里使劲地撬保温罩。

他抬手替鸟掀开了。

白粼粼不由得脑袋探了过去，但被一把握住了，拿开。

少年拉开椅子坐下，看到了桌上的便条：

——阿姨晚上再过来做饭，小宋你放心，我不会和你爸爸说你养小鸟这件事的。

——要开开心心的。

宋郁抬手收了起来，照旧和往常一样，吃完饭，收拾自己的碗筷，上楼，休息。

身后一路跟着只“小鸡”。

白粼粼更多的其实还是好奇，因为宋郁一看就是少爷，怎么手腕上有划痕……

鸟很担忧。

他还是不由自主开始跟随行为。

人去卧室，小鸟飞到人肩头上搭乘“便车”。

人去书桌，小鸟叼着草稿纸啃啃啃。

人去洗手间，小鸟大摇大摆地也要跟着去……

砰！

门被关上了，鸟爪在地板上滑了下。

白粼粼：“……”

切，不去就不去。

他又飞到了书桌上，兢兢业业地又啃那个封皮，或许是做了鸟了，没有任何烦恼，白粼粼比较热衷于给自己尾羽上插纸条。

好玩。

他没一会就啃得差不多了。

宋郁从洗手间出来的时候，垂眸看着那本没有封皮的教辅书，沉默了一会。

总之是相安无事了几天。

人上学，鸟在家自由活动。

都很平静。

但变故发生在周末的那天。

是个阴天，外面在下雨，白粼粼本来是窝在书桌上的笔筒的，毛绒绒的像个挂件。

鸟眼也是闭着的。

主要是因为不分昼夜偷偷打游戏的，他困得要死。

宋郁的号根本就是消遣用的，他从来不看历史战绩，也不在意分段，而这恰恰给了鸟可乘之机。

但还是有点麻烦的，因为键位离的远，鸟腿要劈叉，打完一局酸酸的。

翅根也酸酸的。

宋郁本来是在看书，垂眸看了眼手机屏幕，不知道是看到什么了，扯了扯唇，面色有些冷。

然后起身出门了。

抽走了笔筒的工笔刀。

鸟本来也要去，都歪歪扭扭站在“人”的肩膀了，但还是被一把握住拿下来了，又给放到了笔筒里。

困乏极了，鸟又打了个哈欠。

朦胧之中，白粼粼似乎感觉有手指在自己的喙上戳了下，耳边有微凉的声音：

“我出门一趟。”

后面的事情不太清晰了，只是记得宋郁回来的时候很晚了，浑身湿透，皮肤冷白，指尖有血顺着往下滴。

当时阿姨正好在准备晚饭，吓得不轻，着急去拿绷带处理了。

白粼粼站在桌上，来回走了几圈，最后飞到了少年的肩头。

但还没来得及啾啾。

“我身上湿，待会再上来好不好？”

宋郁侧眸看了过去，语调温和，神色看着很是平静，丝毫不像是刚刚在外面自残过。

白粼粼判断了下，觉得他可能是见了什么人。

但还没来得及仔细思考，鸟被身后的人拿了下来。

阿姨面色很是担忧，一边抽空用手指摸了摸小鸟脑袋，一边拿出来绷带给宋郁缠手上的伤口。

其实动作很熟练。

少年本来是垂眸看着伤口的，但是后面突兀地转头，看着鸟。

白粼粼：“……”

孩子，你这很严重好不好？

看我干什么？

白粼粼尽管不太了解现在的青春期小朋友，但他还是梳理了下翅膀，慢吞吞地往桌边挪动，鸟腿一点点地伸了过去。

羽毛蓬松。

贴了过来。

宋郁受伤的是左手，右手在桌面上放着，他正在低头看着鸟。

流血了。

它不害怕么？

白粼粼仰头看了过去，也就在对视的时候，宋郁语气没有任何起伏地道：

“张姨。”

“我妈妈二胎出生了。”
chunks.englishText:
When Song Yu returned at noon, he saw the little bird wearing a yellow bib, struggling to pry open the food warmer on the dining table.

He raised his hand and lifted the lid for the bird.

Bai Linlin couldn't help but poke his head inside, only to be firmly grasped and pulled away.

The young man pulled out a chair and sat down, noticing a note left on the table:

—The auntie will come back tonight to cook. Don't worry, Little Song, I won't tell your father that you're keeping a little bird.

—Be happy.

Song Yu picked it up and put it away. As usual, he finished his meal, cleared his own dishes, and went upstairs to rest.

A "little chick" followed him all the way.

In truth, Bai Linlin was mostly just curious. Song Yu looked every bit the young master, so why were there scars on his wrists?

The bird was worried.

He couldn't help but continue his shadowing behavior.

When the human went to the bedroom, the little bird flew onto his shoulder to catch a "free ride."

When the human went to the desk, the little bird nibbled away at a piece of draft paper.

When the human went to the bathroom, the little bird strutted along, intending to follow him inside as well...

*Bang!*

The door was shut, and the bird's claws skidded on the floor.

Bai Linlin: "..."

*Hmph, fine, see if I care.*

He flew back to the desk and diligently went back to gnawing on the book cover. Perhaps because he was a bird now and had no worries, Bai Linlin had developed a hobby of tucking scraps of paper into his tail feathers.

It was fun.

Before long, he had finished gnawing it to pieces.

When Song Yu emerged from the bathroom, he looked down at the now coverless textbook and fell silent for a moment.

All in all, things remained peaceful for a few days.

The human went to school, and the bird had free rein at home.

Everything was calm.

But the change occurred on the weekend.

It was an overcast day, and it was raining outside. Bai Linlin had been curled up in the pen holder on the desk, looking like a fluffy little ornament.

His bird eyes were closed.

Mainly because he had been secretly playing video games all night, he was sleepy as hell.

Song Yu’s account was meant for casual play; he never checked his match history or cared about his rank, which was exactly what gave the bird his chance.

It was still a bit troublesome, though, because the keys were far apart, forcing the bird to do the splits with his legs. By the end of a match, he was sore.

Even the roots of his wings ached.

Song Yu had been reading, but he lowered his eyes to look at his phone screen. He didn't know what he saw, but he curled his lips, his expression turning cold.

Then, he got up and headed out.

He took the craft knife from the pen holder with him.

The bird had intended to go along, and was already standing unsteadily on the "human's" shoulder, but he was firmly grasped, taken down, and placed back into the pen holder.

Exhausted, the bird yawned again.

In his hazy state, Bai Linlin felt a finger poke his beak, and a cool, quiet voice reached his ears:

"I'm going out for a bit."

The events that followed were a blur. He only remembered that Song Yu returned very late, soaked to the bone. His skin was a deathly pale, and blood was dripping from his fingertips.

The auntie happened to be preparing dinner and was terrified, rushing to grab bandages to treat him.

Bai Linlin stood on the table, pacing back and forth a few times before finally flying onto the young man’s shoulder.

But before he could even chirp:

"I'm all wet. Can you wait a little while before coming up?"

Song Yu glanced over, his tone gentle and his expression looking perfectly calm, not at all like someone who had just been self-harming outside.

Bai Linlin assessed the situation and figured he must have met someone.

But before he could think it through, he was lifted down by the person behind him.

The auntie looked deeply worried; while using her fingers to stroke the little bird's head, she used her other hand to wrap the bandages around Song Yu's wounds.

Her movements were actually quite practiced.

The young man had been looking down at his wounds, but suddenly, he turned his head to look at the bird.

Bai Linlin: "..."

*Kid, this is pretty serious, you know?*

*Why are you looking at me?*

Although Bai Linlin didn't quite understand the current generation of teenagers, he smoothed his feathers and shuffled slowly toward the edge of the table, his bird legs stretching out bit by bit.

His feathers were fluffy.

He pressed himself against the young man.

Song Yu’s left hand was injured, so his right hand was resting on the table. He was looking down at the bird.

It was bleeding.

Was it not afraid?

Bai Linlin looked up, and just as their eyes met, Song Yu said in a voice devoid of any inflection:

"Auntie Zhang."

"My mother has given birth to her second child."

chunks.chineseText:
第7章

别墅外头还在下雨。

宋郁在椅子上坐着，身上单薄，垂眸看着鸟，静静地道：

“她都三十九了。”

白粼粼鸟眼都瞪大了点，这不是高龄产妇么？

但阿姨闻言也只是怔了下，张了张嘴，也不知道说什么，最后选择岔开话题了：

“外头这么凉，快去冲个热水澡。”

“要注意别碰手啊。”

宋郁面色冷白，不知道在想什么，似乎是觉得没意思，过了一会起身去楼上了。

鸟本来也打算跟上去的，但是被阿姨给留下来擦鸟爪了。

白粼粼残留点人的生活习惯，索性直接坐在桌子上了，爪子被捏住了。

阿姨愁容满面的，叹了口气，自言自语道：

“都离婚十多年了，要是不管就彻底别联系……”

“非让孩子过去做什么。”

“这不是剜人的心么。”

白粼粼其实还是有些意外的，“离婚”他其实可以猜到，毕竟这个房子好像只有宋郁一个人住。

但是，离婚十多年了？

那二胎……

宋郁这个说法，有把自己算在内吗？

鸟心里有个隐隐的猜想，不自觉地仰头往楼上看，然后扑棱翅膀飞过去了。

与此同时，国外。

陈开鹤是在S州的私立医院里得知宋郁母亲又生了一个孩子的消息的，那张打了码的合照都传到文娱榜头条了。

老头儿面色很是铁青，当即就和宋郁的姥爷打了越洋电话。

“江连成，你怎么教你女儿的，她是不是有病！”

江连成是南市有名的书画家，也是宋郁母亲江芮的父亲，最近刚上任美术协会的副主席，正是春风得意的时候。

现下被这么一阵吼，他好半天没反应过来，过了一会才迟疑地问：

“你说芮芮？”

江芮早年同宋父离婚后，消沉了几年，而后看上一个娱乐圈的制片人。

这本无可厚非。

但问题是那男人爱营销家庭美满人设，每次都会让江芮在聚会上带上她与前夫的儿子，不经意让媒体拍摄些照片，造舆论，借机宣传自己的影视剧。

很令人作呕的行为。

第一次是在宋郁读小学的时候，那时孩子很小，正是思念妈妈的时候，江芮很轻而易举就把人接走了。

隔天照片就爆出来了，是在一个包厢里，小小的孩子坐在一旁，旁边是自己微微显怀的母亲和陌生的男人。

宋郁回到家就被父亲扇了一巴掌，指责他是吃里爬外的东西。

可这对于一个想要妈妈的孩子来说，是无妄之灾。

宋郁也是在那时才知道，那些“离婚了我也是你爸爸妈妈”的话，通通都是骗人的。

经年累月，一朝一岁。

江芮再婚都是很久远的事了，算上今年的这一胎，刚好为那制片人添了一对儿女了。

但不知道她是后知后觉自己还有个儿子，还是单纯想要讨好现任丈夫，在前几天的满月酒上又邀请了宋郁。

阖家团圆，留影纪念。

陈开鹤当时看到头条的照片就恼火得不行，整篇文章几乎都在写那制片人的作品，还明里暗里写了“华秉产业”的股份动荡一事，完全是故意的。

现在宋家这个局势，华秉真去发律师函，是把江芮这个生母放在什么位置？

不告。

那其实就是放任“伤害”。

江芮不可能不知道宋郁生病了，或者说，她从头到尾都觉得那是在博关注。

不然不会时隔多年，让媒体再发第二次合影。

“不然呢！老宋是植物人了，不是死了。”

陈开鹤听到对面那不确定的语气就恼火，装什么不知道，又道：

“他就这么一个孙子！”

宋郁的爷爷是宋峥国，早年从军，中年从商，一手创办了华秉实业，是实打实的白手起家。

但也正是因为经历的坎坷，导致他尤为看不惯三心二意的人，自从儿子儿媳离婚后，就始终不同意儿子再婚。

理由是宋郁还太小。

即使后面闹出来私生子丑闻，宋峥国也依然铁血不认，甚至架空了儿子在华秉的权力，大有要修改遗产分配书的意思。

但就在这个紧要关头，宋峥国却在家中心脑血管疾病复发，救治不及时，成了植物人，至今仍在S州疗养。

“师兄，你别急……”

江连成此刻在书房，面色也是有点难看，只能先出声安抚道。

没办法，陈开鹤对他有知遇之恩，当年自己岌岌无名的时候，是靠着对方一路引荐，他才能有现在的名气。

也才……高攀上宋家。

尽管现在是“三十年河西”了，但还是要面上过得去，不能给落人话柄，他斟酌了下，试着说道：

“我回头，不，我现在就去给江芮打电话，让她好好反省反省！”

陈开鹤一听这话就知道是敷衍，尽管气得没办法，但也没失了理智，闭了闭眼把电话给撂了。

这都什么人……

真是可怜了老宋。

生出来的儿子巴不得自己永远植物人；疼爱的孙子被他父亲困在南市、连来探望也做不到。

宋家简直是反了天了。

陈开鹤愈发不后悔自己独身主义的选择，要是他晚年面临峥国这样子的烂摊子。

他就不是植物人了。

他直接死。

-

锦园。

白粼粼其实还是没太理清楚宋家的人物关系，因为他目前见到的宋家人……只有宋郁一个。

其余一概不知。

但自从那天淋雨之后，他就发现少年更加沉默寡言了，有好几次都忘记给他添粮了。

宋郁可能也注意到了自己的反常，于是同阿姨说了帮忙照看小鸟的事，还给转了几千块，但阿姨没要。

白粼粼其实觉得自己根本不需要照顾，因为他最近过得很是滋润。

托宋郁的福，他这几天吃了鸡蛋卷饼、牛肉酥、青椒炒饭、杨枝甘露、鲜鱼丸、糖醋排骨……

一套流程是这样的，鸟在玄关目送阿姨离开，飞到桌子上，身躯下压，用短短的喙开始撬保温罩，钻进去。

而后开启美食之旅。

白粼粼简直叨得不知天地为何物，但他还是有分寸的，偷吃完会小心翼翼把饭菜恢复原状。

具体表现为：

把三块排骨凑成一盘菜。

不过宋郁压根没有发现，或者说是根本没有精力在意，他很明显地消沉了下来。

是抑郁期。

他的注意力持续下降。

一天晚上，别墅里很是安静。

宋郁在餐厅吃饭。

“啾啾？”

鸟飞了过来，板板正正地站在“人”的筷子上……

开始往下滑溜。

白粼粼最后爪子歪歪扭扭的，勉强卡在宋郁的虎口上。

“你是不是变重了点？”

宋郁身着黑色毛衣，高领修身，垂眸看着手背上的小鸟，眼皮掀开了点，轻声道。

白粼粼：“……”

你再说，再说我就下来了啊。

宋郁看了很久，而后用手指碰了碰小鸟胸前的羽毛，力道不轻不重，白粼粼一开始还扭了扭身子，之后就彻底不动了。

因为还挺舒服的。

鸟眯了眯眼，非常满意。

但就在这时。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 7

Rain was still pouring outside the villa.

Song Yu sat in a chair, dressed in thin layers, lowering his gaze toward the bird as he said quietly,

"She is already thirty-nine."

The bird Bailinlin widened its eyes slightly. Wasn't that considered an advanced maternal age?

Yet the housekeeper only paused momentarily at these words, her lips parting as if she didn't know what to say, before finally opting to change the subject.

"It's so chilly outside. Go take a hot shower."

"Be careful not to get your hands wet."

With a pale, cold expression and lost in thought, Song Yu seemed to find the conversation pointless. After a moment, he got up and headed upstairs.

The bird originally intended to follow him, but the housekeeper intercepted it to wipe its claws.

Retaining a few human habits, Bailinlin simply sat down on the table while its claws were gently held.

With a face full of sorrow, the housekeeper let out a sigh and muttered to herself,

"They've been divorced for over a decade. If they didn't care, they should have cut ties completely..."

"Why on earth must she drag the child into this?"

"Isn't this just carving out a piece of someone's heart?"

Bailinlin was actually quite surprised. He had managed to guess the "divorce" part, especially since this house seemed to be lived in by Song Yu alone.

However, divorced for over a decade?

Then what about this second child...

Did Song Yu's previous statement include himself in that equation?

A faint notion flickered in the bird's heart. Without thinking, it raised its head to look upstairs, then flapped its wings and flew up.

Meanwhile, overseas.

Chen Kaihe received the news in a private hospital in State S that Song Yu's mother had given birth to another child, with a mosaic-blurred group photo plastered all over the entertainment headline rankings.

The old man's face turned livid, and he immediately placed a transatlantic call to Song Yu's maternal grandfather.

"Jiang Liancheng, how on earth did you raise your daughter? Has she lost her mind?!"

Jiang Liancheng was a renowned calligrapher and painter in Nanshi, as well as the father of Song Yu's mother, Jiang Rui. Having recently assumed office as the vice chairman of the Fine Arts Association, he was currently riding the crest of success.

Blasted by this sudden roar, he took a long time to react before asking hesitantly,

"Are you talking about Ruirui?"

After divorcing Song Yu's father in her early years, Jiang Rui had spent a few years feeling low before taking a fancy to a producer in the entertainment industry.

In itself, this was hardly objectionable.

The problem, however, was that the man loved to market a persona of domestic bliss, invariably making Jiang Rui bring her ex-husband's son along to gatherings and subtly prompting the media to snap photos to stir up public opinion and promote his film and television projects.

It was a truly sickening behavior.

The first time had been while Song Yu was in primary school. Back then, the child was very young and deeply missed his mother, so Jiang Rui had easily managed to take him away.

The next day, photos exploded across the internet. They were taken in a private dining room, with the tiny child sitting off to the side, flanked by his mother—whose belly was slightly swelling with pregnancy—and a strange man.

Upon returning home, Song Yu had received a slap across the face from his father, who accused him of being ungrateful and siding with outsiders.

Yet for a child who simply longed for his mother, this was an undeserved disaster.

It was then that Song Yu learned those comforting words—"Even if we're divorced, I'm still your mom and dad"—were absolute lies.

Year after year, day by day.

Jiang Rui's remarriage was a matter of the distant past; counting this year's child, she had given the producer a pair of children.

Yet whether she had belatedly remembered she still had a son, or simply wished to curry favor with her current husband, she had invited Song Yu to the baby's one-month celebration a few days ago.

A picture-perfect family reunion, captured on film for posterity.

Seeing the headline photo at the time, Chen Kaihe had been utterly enraged. Nearly the entire article was dedicated to praising the producer's works, while also alluding directly and indirectly to the stock volatility of "Huabing Industries"—it was entirely deliberate.

Given the current political climate of the Song family, if Huabing truly issued a lawyer's letter, where would it leave Jiang Rui, the birth mother?

To not sue.

That was essentially condoning "harm."

Jiang Rui could not possibly be unaware that Song Yu was ill; or rather, she had believed from the very beginning that he was merely doing it for attention.

Otherwise, after all these years, she would never have allowed the media to publish a second group photo.

"Of course she does! Old Song is in a vegetative state, not dead!"

Hearing the uncertain tone on the other end, Chen Kaihe grew even angrier. Why was the man feigning ignorance? He pressed on,

"He is his only grandson!"

Song Yu's grandfather was Song Zhengguo, who had served in the military in his youth and entered the business world in middle age, single-handedly founding Huabing Industries through sheer grit and a blank slate.

Yet precisely because of his arduous journey, he harbored a profound aversion to fickle people. Ever since his son and daughter-in-law divorced, he had steadfastly refused to let his son remarry.

His reasoning was that Song Yu was still too far young.

Even when the illegitimate child scandal broke out later on, Song Zhengguo remained iron-fisted in his refusal to acknowledge them, eventually stripping his son of his authority within Huabing and heavily implying an intent to rewrite his will.

Yet right at this critical juncture, Song Zhengguo suffered a recurrence of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease at home. Untreated in time, he fell into a vegetative state and was still convalescing in State S to this day.

"Senior Brother, don't be rash..."

In his study, Jiang Liancheng wore an equally unsightly expression as he hurriedly tried to offer soothing words.

There was no help for it. Chen Kaihe was his benefactor; back when he was obscure and insignificant, it was thanks to the other man's repeated referrals that he had attained his current fame.

And had managed to... climb so high as to marry into the Song family.

Though the tides had turned over the past thirty years, he still needed to maintain a facade and avoid giving others grounds for gossip. Pondering for a moment, he cautiously offered,

"I'll turn around—no, I'll call Jiang Rui right now and make her reflect deeply on herself!"

Hearing this, Chen Kaihe knew it was merely perfunctory stalling. Though furious beyond measure, he retained his reason, closed his eyes, and slammed the phone down.

What kind of people were these...

It truly was a pity for Old Song.

The son he bore wished nothing more than for him to remain a vegetable forever; the grandson he cherished was trapped in Nanshi by his father, unable even to pay a visit.

The Song family had truly turned upside down.

Chen Kaihe grew increasingly unwavering in his choice of lifelong celibacy. If he had to face such a tangled mess of troubles in his old age like Zhengguo did...

He wouldn't become a vegetable.

He'd just die straight away.

-

Jin Yuan.

Bailinlin still hadn't quite sorted out the web of relationships in the Song family, primarily because the only member of the Song family he had laid eyes on thus far... was Song Yu himself.

He knew nothing of the rest.

However, ever since getting caught in the rain that day, he noticed that the young man had grown even more taciturn, on several occasions forgetting to refill his food bowl.

Song Yu likely realized his own absent-mindedness, as he had instructed the housekeeper to help look after the little bird and even transferred a few thousand yuan to her, though she refused to take it.

Bailinlin actually felt he required no care at all, living quite luxuriously as of late.

Thanks to Song Yu, over the past few days he had feasted upon egg-wrapped pancakes, beef pastries, green pepper fried rice, *yangzhi ganlu*, fresh fish balls, sweet and sour pork ribs...

The routine generally went like this: the bird would see the housekeeper off at the entryway, fly onto the table, flatten its body, and use its short beak to pry open the insulation cover before tunneling inside.

Thus began a culinary tour.

Bailinlin pecked away with wild abandon, oblivious to the world, yet he retained a shred of restraint: after secret snacking, he would meticulously restore the dishes to their original state.

Specifically manifested as:

Piecing three leftover ribs back together to form a cohesive dish on the plate.

Yet Song Yu remained completely oblivious—or perhaps lacked the energy to care. His depression had clearly deepened.

He was in a depressive cycle.

His attention span continued to plummet.

One evening, the villa was dead silent.

Song Yu was eating dinner in the dining room.

"Chirp?"

The bird flew over and stood upright and proper right on the "human's" chopstick...

And began sliding downward.

In the end, Bailinlin's claws were crooked, barely managing to hook onto the webbing between Song Yu's thumb and index finger.

"Have you gotten a bit heavier?"

Dressed in a black, high-collared, form-fitting sweater, Song Yu lowered his gaze to the little bird on the back of his hand, lifting his eyelids slightly as he said softly,

Bailinlin: "..."

If you say that again—say that one more time and I'm getting down right now.

Song Yu stared for a long time, then used a finger to lightly stroke the feathers on the little bird's chest with moderate pressure. At first, Bailinlin squirmed a little before completely freezing.

Because it felt quite nice.

The bird narrowed its eyes in utter satisfaction.

Yet right at that moment—

chunks.chineseText:
少年蹙眉喃喃道：“是刀胸吗？”

白粼粼愣了下，这是什么东西？

宋郁查过鹦鹉的饲养知识，刀胸是一种疾病，多发于营养不良的小鸟，说是胸部位置像是一把刀。

白粼粼被拿了下来，然后感觉是被拍了照，宋郁修长的手指在手机屏幕上滑动。

鸟好奇，探头去看。

发现是“人”发了个帖子：

【这是刀胸了么？】

宋郁的确不想一直麻烦齐思扬，对方还有学业在身，他索性想着在网上问一问。

不过在等评论的时候，小鸟已经站在了他的袖子上，脑袋圆圆的，往下认真地看。

宋郁几乎走了下神。

帖子此刻有了几条评论：

【咦惹，这么肥美。】

下面紧跟着回复：

【小鸡别看是恶评。】

但白粼粼已经看到了，爪子都踩得用力了点，仰头就一顿抗议：

“啾啾啾啾！”

“啾啾啾！”

[胡说八道！]

[鸟不胖！]

宋郁其实难免有些错觉，它是……看得懂么？

修长的手指又滑动了下，但就在这时，鸟腿一伸，卡住了。

白粼粼又在低头看评论。

【呃呃，瘦得凸起是刀胸，胖得凹陷是肥缝。】

“啾啾啾啾！”

“啾啾啾啾啾！”

宋郁也听不懂，但能判断出他的小鸟不太乐意看到这些评论，于是把手机关了。

白粼粼很是不高兴，弯腰还叨了下已经黑掉的屏幕，但用力过猛，一脑袋栽进“人”的手掌心。

可那上面还缠着绷带。

白粼粼一下子老实了，他害怕碰到对方的伤口。

爪子都收了收。

但好在宋郁没有什么反应，只是把鸟放到了桌上，垂眸自己看那个帖子。

直到确定是一场乌龙之后，少年才把手机放到了一旁，开始吃已经冷掉的饭菜。

白粼粼歪了歪头，还是没看出来宋郁是个什么心情，只知道大概还是不好。

因为吃的药变多了。

-

大约半个月后，白粼粼意外地发现自己好像学会说话了，这是阿姨不断训练的结果，第一句就是：

“举头望明月。”

很有文化的一只小鸟。

阿姨连连鼓掌，给鸟捧场，还投喂了旺仔小馒头，一个劲地表扬：

“好棒好棒。”

“小宋知道一定很高兴。”

白粼粼鸟脸一红，羽毛蓬松，不好意思再说了。

不过还要旺仔小馒头。

鸟想要，鸟得到。

……

但宋郁的心情似乎仍然没有变好，一连回来几次都只是上楼打游戏，白粼粼一直陪着。

飞到少年肩头，伸着鸟腿，坐下。

直到有一天。

家里的阿姨突然被辞退了，这几乎是一个导火索，宋郁白天打了一通电话，那边好像是他的父亲，少年语气从头到尾都不好：

“这么爱管着我？那你自己怎么不亲自过来呢？”

“还是说，你守着我爷爷，是心里有鬼？”

宋郁身高已经一米八了，坐在岛台那里漫不经心地打电话，手里玩着一把工笔刀。

白粼粼一边偷偷听，一边左右摇摆地走过去，鸟头探了几下，快准狠地——

叼走了“危险玩具”。

宋郁其实是愣了下，连带着输出都停了。

电话那里的声音更加恼火，一连说了好几个“混账”和“无法无天”。

宋郁这才回了回神，抽空说了句：

“谢谢夸奖。”

电话那头的中年男人似乎是破防了，传出来些乱七八糟的杂音，还有一道关门的动静。

宋郁压根就没有在意，他左手的伤已经恢复完全，只是垂着眼皮，定定地看着前方：

桌前的小鸟叼着那把工笔刀，很是勤勤恳恳地往旁边走，或许是因为太沉了，啪嗒啪嗒走两步歇一步的。

最后停下来，鸟头转了转。

似乎是在环顾四周。

确定目标后，它又歪歪扭扭地往桌边走。

爪子并了并，尾羽上翘，开始蓄力。

宋郁就这么看着鸟用力一甩，把工笔刀扔进了垃圾桶里。

不过在鸟转身的时候，他不动声色地收回了目光，喉结微微滚了下。

手机里面仍然有聒噪的声音：

“宋郁！我告诉你，你一点都不如宋阳，亏你还是个哥哥。”

“你爷爷就算是醒了也会对你失望——”

宋郁面色直接变了，站了起来，冷声打断道：“你有什么资格提我爷爷！”

对面一下子安静了下来，好似是反应过来什么。

电话中断了。

白粼粼站在桌面上，安静如鸡。

宋郁情绪确实不好，垂着的手指都生理性地颤了颤，但他深呼吸了下，而后看过去桌面，恢复成正常的语气：

“对不起。”

“我把你的朋友弄丢了。”

白粼粼其实是愣了下的，朋友？说的是阿姨吗？

可是，他是他的小鸟。

没有宋郁，阿姨是不会来做饭的。

白粼粼还是想不通，直到宋郁伸过来一根手指，鸟自然而然抬腿上去了。

脑袋圆圆的。

鸟歪了歪头。

“我总是陪不了你很长时间。”

白粼粼闻言一下子警觉了起来，什么情况，不取名字是这个原因？

宋郁本来还想多解释几句，但唇角突然被创了一下，鸟已经扑棱翅膀飞过来了。

有钝钝的冲击力。

“啾啾啾啾。”

“啾啾啾。”

宋郁抬手接住了小鸟，低头问：“你自己在家里不会孤单么？”

白粼粼：“……”

不孤单，有吃有喝，有wifi。

当然，如果“人”愿意为鸟买一部手机的话，那就更好了。

白粼粼想到这里，脑海又自动浮现一串密码：

[******]

太堕落了，怎么能记得这么牢固……

宋郁其实不知道鸟的心理活动，他只是觉得他的小鸟会有些孤单。

大约晚上八点钟的时候，有人送过来新的鸟笼。

这已经是第九个窝了。

内部有木头制的小架子，还有栖杆，用来打发时间的麦秸秆、谷物棒等等，几乎一应俱全。

宋郁附身蹲在地板上，侧眸看着肩头的小鸟，其实有些无措。

它始终不进笼子。

“还是不喜欢？”

白粼粼点了点头，羽毛丰盈，像个毛球。

宋郁唇角微微压直，最终还是回了卧室，鸟扑棱翅膀就飞了下来。

站在了纸巾盒里。

“……”

齐思扬同他说过和尚鹦鹉的常见睡姿是没有仰躺的，陈爷爷也发过来了一些专业养鸟文件。

他不知道怎么办。

但也就这么一会儿，宋郁再低头去看，鸟已经躺下了。

安寝。

纸巾盒四四方方的，里面有个两脚朝天的鸟。

“。”

不太吉利的样子。

……

阿姨是因为没有及时传消息而被辞退的，宋启明，也就是宋郁的父亲，即使远在国外，也始终监控着自己的儿子。

或许是因为得知宋郁再次参加他母亲的“家庭聚会”过于恼火，倒是给直接忘了责问“养鸟这一事。

相安无事了几天。
chunks.englishText:
The young man frowned and muttered, "Is it keel deformity?"

Bai Linlin was stunned. What on earth was that?

Song Yu had looked up parrot care knowledge. Keel deformity was a condition common in malnourished birds, where the chest area becomes sharp and prominent, resembling the edge of a knife.

Bai Linlin was set down and felt as though a photo had been taken of him; Song Yu’s slender fingers swiped across his phone screen.

The bird was curious and craned his neck to look.

He discovered that "the human" had posted on a forum:

[Is this keel deformity?]

Song Yu truly didn't want to keep bothering Qi Siyang, who still had his studies to attend to, so he simply decided to ask online.

However, while waiting for comments, the little bird had already landed on his sleeve, his head round and fluffy, looking down intently.

Song Yu was momentarily distracted.

The post already had a few comments:

[Whoa, so plump and delicious.]

Immediately followed by a reply:

[Don't look at the mean comments, little chicken.]

But Bai Linlin had already seen it. He stomped his claws a little harder, tilted his head back, and protested loudly:

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

"Chirp chirp!"

[Nonsense!]

[The bird is not fat!]

Song Yu couldn't help but have an illusion: could it... actually understand?

His slender fingers swiped again, but just then, the bird’s leg stretched out and got stuck.

Bai Linlin was looking down at the comments again.

[Uh, thin with a protruding bone is keel deformity; fat with a sunken center is a fat crease.]

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

Song Yu couldn't understand, but he could tell his little bird wasn't happy seeing these comments, so he turned off the phone.

Bai Linlin was very displeased. He bent down and pecked at the now-dark screen, but used too much force and face-planted into the "human's" palm.

But it was still wrapped in bandages.

Bai Linlin immediately behaved, afraid of touching the other’s wound.

He even retracted his claws.

Fortunately, Song Yu didn't react, simply placing the bird on the table and lowering his eyes to read the post himself.

Only after confirming it was a false alarm did the young man put the phone aside and begin to eat his now-cold meal.

Bai Linlin tilted his head. He still couldn't tell what kind of mood Song Yu was in, only that it probably wasn't good.

Because the amount of medicine he had to take had increased.

-

About half a month later, Bai Linlin accidentally discovered that he seemed to have learned how to speak. This was the result of the auntie's constant training. The first sentence was:

"Raise my head to gaze at the bright moon."

A very cultured little bird.

The auntie clapped repeatedly, cheering for the bird, and even fed him a Wangzai milk bun, praising him incessantly:

"So smart, so smart."

"Little Song will be so happy when he knows."

Bai Linlin’s bird face flushed red, his feathers puffed up, and he was too embarrassed to say it again.

But he still wanted the Wangzai milk bun.

The bird wanted it, the bird got it.

……

But Song Yu’s mood didn't seem to improve. He came home several times just to go upstairs and play games, and Bai Linlin accompanied him the whole time.

He would fly to the young man’s shoulder, stretch out his bird leg, and sit down.

Until one day.

The auntie at home was suddenly dismissed. This was almost a trigger. Song Yu had a phone call during the day, seemingly with his father. The young man’s tone was terrible from start to finish:

"So keen on controlling me? Then why don't you come over yourself?"

"Or is it that you’re keeping watch over my grandfather because you have a guilty conscience?"

Song Yu was already 1.8 meters tall. He sat at the island counter, talking on the phone nonchalantly while playing with a craft knife.

Bai Linlin listened in secretly while waddling back and forth. He poked his head a few times, then—fast, accurate, and ruthless—

He snatched away the "dangerous toy."

Song Yu was actually stunned, his verbal tirade coming to a halt.

The voice on the phone became even more furious, spitting out several "scoundrel" and "lawless" remarks.

Only then did Song Yu snap back to reality, taking a moment to say:

"Thanks for the compliment."

The middle-aged man on the other end seemed to have a breakdown, with chaotic noises coming through, followed by the sound of a door slamming.

Song Yu didn't care at all. The wound on his left hand had fully healed, but he kept his eyelids lowered, staring fixedly ahead:

The little bird on the table was holding the craft knife, diligently walking to the side. Perhaps because it was too heavy, it took two steps and then rested.

Finally, it stopped and turned its head.

It seemed to be surveying its surroundings.

After confirming the target, it waddled toward the edge of the table again.

It brought its claws together, lifted its tail feathers, and began to build up momentum.

Song Yu watched as the bird gave a forceful flick, tossing the craft knife into the trash can.

However, when the bird turned around, he retracted his gaze nonchalantly, his Adam's apple rolling slightly.

The phone still had noisy sounds coming from it:

"Song Yu! I’m telling you, you’re not even half as good as Song Yang. What a waste that you’re the older brother."

"Even if your grandfather wakes up, he’ll be disappointed in you—"

Song Yu’s expression changed instantly. He stood up and interrupted coldly: "What right do you have to mention my grandfather!"

The other side went quiet, as if realizing something.

The call was cut off.

Bai Linlin stood on the table, as quiet as a chicken.

Song Yu was indeed in a bad mood; his hanging fingers trembled physiologically, but he took a deep breath, then looked at the tabletop, returning to a normal tone:

"I'm sorry."

"I lost your friend."

Bai Linlin was actually stunned. A friend? Was he talking about the auntie?

But he was *his* little bird.

Without Song Yu, the auntie wouldn't have come to cook.

Bai Linlin still couldn't figure it out until Song Yu extended a finger, and the bird naturally lifted a leg and stepped onto it.

His head was round.

The bird tilted his head.

"I can never stay with you for very long."

Hearing this, Bai Linlin became alert. What was going on? Was this the reason he wouldn't give him a name?

Song Yu originally wanted to explain more, but his lips were suddenly bumped; the bird had already flapped his wings and flown over.

There was a dull impact.

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp."

"Chirp chirp."

Song Yu raised his hand to catch the little bird and lowered his head to ask: "Don't you feel lonely at home by yourself?"

Bai Linlin: "..."

Not lonely. He had food, drink, and Wi-Fi.

Of course, if "the human" was willing to buy a phone for the bird, that would be even better.

Thinking of this, a string of passwords automatically appeared in Bai Linlin's mind:

[******]

So degenerate. How could he remember it so firmly...

Song Yu didn't know the bird's internal monologue; he just felt that his little bird must be a bit lonely.

Around eight o'clock in the evening, someone delivered a new birdcage.

This was already the ninth nest.

Inside, there were small wooden shelves, perches, straw stalks to pass the time, grain bars, and so on—almost everything one could need.

Song Yu leaned down and squatted on the floor, looking sideways at the little bird on his shoulder, feeling a bit helpless.

It still wouldn't enter the cage.

"Still don't like it?"

Bai Linlin nodded, his feathers plump, looking like a fur ball.

Song Yu’s lips pressed into a thin line, and in the end, he returned to the bedroom. The bird flapped his wings and flew down.

He stood inside a tissue box.

"..."

Qi Siyang had told him that monk parakeets didn't usually sleep lying on their backs, and Grandpa Chen had sent over some professional bird-keeping documents.

He didn't know what to do.

But just a moment later, when Song Yu looked down again, the bird was already lying down.

Sleeping soundly.

The tissue box was square, and inside was a bird with its feet in the air.

"..."

It didn't look very auspicious.

……

The auntie was dismissed because she didn't report news in time. Song Qiming, Song Yu’s father, monitored his son constantly, even from abroad.

Perhaps because he was too furious to learn that Song Yu had attended his mother’s "family gathering" again, he actually forgot to reprimand him about "keeping a bird."

They lived in peace for a few days.

chunks.chineseText:
“其实鹦鹉算是杂食动物，它可能会好奇人吃的东西，卤肉……不是很久之前吃的吗？现在没事就行。”

陈开鹤正在S州的一所档案馆里给宋郁通话，精气神仍然很好，因为医院那里说峥国的身体素质仍然保持得很好，有清醒的可能性。

而锦园这里正是午夜。

宋郁晚上会失眠，他洗完澡，发梢都是潮的，眉眼轮廓在台灯下显得很是清晰。

电话那边还有絮絮叨叨的声音：

“科学喂养是正确的，但是小鸟也没有那么脆弱，南美的和尚鹦鹉也是会叨走人类丢下的食物的。”

“听小齐说你给它买了很多东西？取名字了吗？”

陈开鹤很是慈爱地询问了几句，宋郁生病之后就有些孤僻了，同幼年时期是完全不一样了。

他不可能不心疼。

“没有。”

夜已经很深了，宋郁垂眸看着纸巾盒里的小鸟，心里很平静。

取名字……

“好了，你那边很晚了，早点睡觉。”

“S州这里我看着的，你爷爷没事，不要担心。”

陈开鹤在那边又嘱咐了几句，电话这才挂断。

时间很快来到五月。

宋郁其实找过几次阿姨，给了不少钱，他起初是不喜欢对方总是同宋启明发消息，但后面看到医院里的孩子，什么话也说不出了。

一共给了二十万。

说是鸟的围兜钱。

阿姨眼泪在脸上都划成线了，最后只是握着宋郁的手，嘱咐着要好好生活。

少年割腕过。

宋郁回到了家中，心情不算太好，他没有请回鸟的“朋友”，毕竟他看到过鸟很开心的样子。

现在是假期，别墅里没有其他人，显得倒是空荡荡的。

宋郁走到餐桌那边，不由得蹙眉，因为碟子里的鸟粮还是分毫未动。

或者说，是拨了两下。

好看着已经“动”过了。

鸟在敷衍。

宋郁有些心烦意乱，他试着去好好养，可是总是和教程上的不一样，不知道该怎么做。

也就在这时，楼上有扑棱翅膀的声音，蓝色小鸟从他的卧室里飞出来了。

最后稳稳地降落在“人”的肩头。

白粼粼有些心虚，他刚刚打完一局游戏……

“啾啾。”

宋郁垂眸把鸟拿了下来，面色有些难看，因为小鸟的羽毛边缘有些异常，漂亮的蓝羽主轴那里有横向的黑灰色纹路。

压力纹。

有营养不良的成因，也有情感上的因素。

可是齐思扬已经带过他的师弟来体检，小鸟很健康。

那显而易见是后者。

白粼粼的鸟头被微微卡住，他抽了抽自己的短喙，开始去叨人，不过也没太用力，就是咬一咬。

怎么还不放开他？

宋郁情绪变得很不好，但即使这样，也没有对鸟表露什么情绪，只是碰了碰小鸟的脑袋。

“啾啾啾？”

白粼粼歪了歪鸟头。

大约一个小时后，有些搬运工来了锦园，零零散散地在往二楼的一个房间里搬东西。

宋郁在旁边付了钱，似乎在沟通什么。

鸟刚在厨房转了一圈，现在看着人来人往的，在地板上啪嗒啪嗒地走着，也不想飞。

犹如一个走地鸡。

“结清了结清了。”

“那我们就先走了……”

那群上门送货的人员又都走了，不过转头的时候还吓了一跳，因为鸟在地上，仰头看着他们，挡住路了。

宋郁面色温和，只是半蹲把手伸过去了，鸟很自然地抬了抬腿，站得稳稳当当。

起驾。

“不好意思，它不喜欢笼子，就在外面玩。”

工作人员点了点头，表示理解，不过走的时候还是感叹：

这年头，鸟都有独立房间了……

是的，宋郁直接让人过来安装了一套类似于攀爬架的木头装置，上面还有各种各样的小树屋，房间里的空调全程开着。

很豪华了。

但结果仍然不算太好，鸟只是在房间里飞了一圈，叼着一根麦秸秆回来了，站在宋郁肩头上。

圆滚滚的脑袋歪了歪。

又兢兢业业地把麦秸杆插在自己尾羽上了。

白粼粼的想法很简单，他又没有口袋，要么只能一路叼着，要么插身上去。

但他没想到的是——

“是发情了吗？”

宋郁原来也见过小鸟往自己尾羽里插纸条，当时他有查过，说是准备筑巢的行为。

但这多发于母鸟身上。

“啾啾啾啾！！啾啾啾！”

白粼粼整个鸟都红温了，说的什么话，说的什么话！

他直接一顿哐哐叫，而后很用力地叨了一口宋郁的手，飞到门外去了。

宋郁有些愣，手指流血了。

它好生气。

但他又觉得正常，可能发情期情绪不好……

可爱。

事情并没有那么容易过去，宋郁发现鸟在和他生气，一整个周末，没有靠近过来。

只是啪嗒啪嗒在地上走。

毛茸茸的。

宋郁不知道怎么办，他没有和小鸟沟通的经验。

尤其是好几天，它都不吃鸟粮的情况。

宋郁的确开始有些失控，他也没有怎么吃饭，而是很担心鸟会死掉。

情绪也很消沉。

但白粼粼其实根本就没有绝食的意思，他已经完全熟悉了这个别墅的构造，吃零食简直是熟门熟路的。

鸟圆嘟嘟的。

丝毫不瘦。

就是还是很生气！

宋郁一个小孩子，怎么能说那种话！

白粼粼虽然是鸟的身躯，但是他的内心仍然是个“成年人”，被那么一说……像被调戏了一样。

母胎单身需要缓好几天。

但他不知道的是，宋郁已经因为这件事吃了翻倍的药了，几乎出现了视力模糊的情况。

饲养宠物的确有助于心理调节。

但一旦死亡或者被宠物拒绝靠近，会起到极大的反作用。

白粼粼忘记自己没有吃鸟粮这件事了，但这在宋郁看来，是绝食。

此刻是中午，卧室门始终是开着的。

宋郁在房间里打游戏，面色冷白，电脑页面不断切换，挂脖耳机里传来一些击杀的通报。

他的心脏在很快地跳动，视野也变得模糊，头晕目眩。

养不好。

就是养不好。

宋郁起身仰躺在床上，手盖住了眼睛，视野里的黑色物质在翻涌、扭动……几乎完全覆了过来。

为什么要活着呢？

谁在乎。

身体像是灌了铅，四肢被看不见的东西困住，灵魂被分割的支离破碎。

宋郁昏沉之际，想起来那只在秋水巷撞过来的小鸟，温热的身躯，手指那些微微的啄感……

意识坠了下去。

与此同时，白粼粼已经在卧室门口鬼鬼祟祟了，他已经好些天没打游戏了。

鸟爱面子，鸟偷偷来打。

白粼粼先是探了探头，左右环顾了下，看到了“人”在床上睡觉才大摇大摆地往里面走。

啪嗒啪嗒的。

活脱脱一个走地鸡。

白粼粼扑棱翅膀飞到了椅子上，发现了耳机，里面还有游戏待机的声音，鸟很羡慕。

这个世界上不能研发一下给鸟用的耳机吗？小一号就行。
chunks.englishText:
"Actually, parrots are omnivores. It might be curious about human food. Braised meat... didn't you eat that a long time ago? It's fine as long as it's okay now."

Chen Kaihe was talking to Song Yu from an archive in S Province. He was still in high spirits because the hospital said that Zheng Guo’s physical condition remained very good, and there was a possibility of him waking up.

And here in Jinyuan, it was midnight.

Song Yu suffered from insomnia at night. He had just showered, his hair tips still damp, and his facial contours looked very sharp under the desk lamp.

There was still chattering on the other end of the line:

"Scientific feeding is correct, but the little bird isn't that fragile. Monk parakeets in South America will also snatch food dropped by humans."

"I heard from Little Qi that you bought it a lot of things? Did you give it a name?"

Chen Kaihe asked with great affection. Song Yu had become somewhat reclusive after falling ill, completely different from his childhood.

He couldn't help but feel heartbroken.

"No."

The night was already very deep. Song Yu lowered his eyes to look at the little bird in the tissue box, his heart very calm.

Giving a name...

"Alright, it's very late there, go to sleep early."

"I'm watching things here in S Province. Your grandfather is fine, don't worry."

Chen Kaihe gave a few more instructions before the call ended.

Time quickly arrived in May.

Song Yu had actually looked for the auntie a few times and given her quite a bit of money. At first, he didn't like that she always sent messages to Song Qiming, but later, seeing the children in the hospital, he couldn't say anything.

He gave a total of two hundred thousand.

He called it money for the bird's bib.

Tears streaked down the auntie's face, and in the end, she just held Song Yu’s hand, urging him to live well.

The young man had once slit his wrists.

Song Yu returned home, his mood not particularly good. He didn't invite the bird’s "friend" back; after all, he had seen how happy the bird was.

It was vacation time now, and there was no one else in the villa, making it feel empty.

Song Yu walked to the dining table and couldn't help but frown, because the bird food in the dish remained untouched.

Or rather, it had been poked at twice.

Just enough to look like it had been "touched."

The bird was just going through the motions.

Song Yu felt a bit agitated. He tried to raise it properly, but it was always different from the tutorials, and he didn't know what to do.

Just then, there was the sound of flapping wings upstairs, and the little blue bird flew out of his bedroom.

Finally, it landed steadily on "the human's" shoulder.

Bai Linlin felt a bit guilty. He had just finished a game...

"Chirp."

Song Yu lowered his eyes and took the bird down, his expression looking quite ugly, because the edges of the little bird's feathers were abnormal. The beautiful blue feather shafts had horizontal black-gray markings.

Stress bars.

There were causes related to malnutrition, but also emotional factors.

But Qi Siyang had already brought his junior to give it a check-up, and the little bird was very healthy.

Then it was obviously the latter.

Bai Linlin’s bird head was slightly held, and he pulled his short beak, starting to peck at the human, though not too hard—just a little bite.

Why wouldn't he let him go?

Song Yu’s emotions became very bad, but even so, he didn't show any emotion toward the bird, only touching the little bird’s head.

"Chirp chirp chirp?"

Bai Linlin tilted his bird head.

About an hour later, some movers came to Jinyuan, scattering things into a room on the second floor.

Song Yu paid them nearby, seemingly communicating something.

The bird had just circled the kitchen and was now watching the people coming and going, walking *patter-patter* on the floor, not wanting to fly.

Like a free-range chicken.

"Settled, settled."

"Then we'll be going..."

The group of delivery workers were startled when they turned around because the bird was on the ground, looking up at them, blocking the way.

Song Yu’s expression was gentle; he just half-squatted and extended his hand. The bird naturally lifted a leg and stood firmly.

"Sorry, it doesn't like cages, so it plays outside."

The staff nodded, indicating they understood, but as they left, they still sighed:

These days, birds even have their own independent rooms...

Yes, Song Yu had people come to install a set of wooden devices similar to a climbing frame, with all kinds of small treehouses, and the air conditioning in the room was kept on the whole time.

It was very luxurious.

But the result was still not very good. The bird just flew around the room, came back with a straw stalk, and stood on Song Yu’s shoulder.

His round head tilted.

And then he diligently stuck the straw stalk into his own tail feathers.

Bai Linlin’s idea was very simple. He didn't have pockets, so he either had to carry it in his beak the whole way or stick it on his body.

But what he didn't expect was—

"Is it in heat?"

Song Yu had seen the little bird tucking paper strips into his tail feathers before. He had looked it up at the time, and it was said to be nesting behavior.

But this was more common in female birds.

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp!! Chirp chirp chirp!"

Bai Linlin turned red all over. What was he saying? What was he saying!

He let out a series of loud chirps, then gave Song Yu’s hand a very forceful peck and flew out the door.

Song Yu was stunned; his finger was bleeding.

It was so angry.

But he also felt it was normal; maybe it was in a bad mood due to the heat cycle...

Cute.

Things didn't pass that easily. Song Yu found that the bird was angry with him. For the entire weekend, it didn't come near him.

It just walked *patter-patter* on the ground.

Fluffy.

Song Yu didn't know what to do. He had no experience communicating with a little bird.

Especially since it hadn't eaten any bird food for several days.

Song Yu did indeed start to lose control. He didn't eat much either, worried that the bird would die.

His mood was also very depressed.

But Bai Linlin actually had no intention of fasting at all. He was already completely familiar with the layout of this villa and knew his way around the snacks perfectly.

The bird was chubby.

Not thin at all.

He was just still very angry!

How could a kid like Song Yu say such things!

Although Bai Linlin was in a bird’s body, his heart was still an "adult." Being told that... it felt like being teased.

A lifelong single person needed a few days to recover.

But what he didn't know was that Song Yu had taken double the medicine because of this, almost to the point of blurred vision.

Keeping pets did help with psychological regulation.

But once death occurred or the pet refused to come near, it would have a huge counterproductive effect.

Bai Linlin forgot that he hadn't eaten bird food, but to Song Yu, it was a hunger strike.

It was noon, and the bedroom door was always open.

Song Yu was playing games in the room, his face cold and pale. The computer page kept switching, and the sound of kill notifications came through his headset.

His heart was beating very fast, his vision becoming blurred, and he felt dizzy.

He couldn't raise it well.

He just couldn't raise it well.

Song Yu got up and lay back on the bed, covering his eyes with his hand. The black substance in his vision was churning and twisting... almost completely covering him.

Why live?

Who cares.

His body felt like it was filled with lead, his limbs trapped by something invisible, his soul shattered into pieces.

In his drowsy state, Song Yu remembered the little bird that had crashed into him in Qiu Shui Lane, its warm body, the slight pecking sensation on his fingers...

His consciousness sank.

At the same time, Bai Linlin was already sneaking around the bedroom door. He hadn't played games for several days.

The bird was proud; the bird was coming to play in secret.

Bai Linlin first poked his head in, looked left and right, and saw "the human" sleeping on the bed before walking in grandly.

*Patter-patter.*

A proper free-range chicken.

Bai Linlin flapped his wings and flew onto the chair, discovering the headset. There was still the sound of the game on standby, and the bird was very envious.

Couldn't this world invent a headset for birds? A smaller size would do.

chunks.chineseText:
不过他没有太浪费时间，而是伸了伸鸟腿，挪动了下鼠标，嚯，他战绩不错。

白粼粼一时半会入了神，火速开了一局，反正宋郁吃了药都会睡得很久的。

大不了一会立马飞走。

鸟开始紧张刺激地打游戏。

咳咳。

鸟时不时地回头看一眼床，有种偷情的感觉，身上的压力纹又深了一些。

但时局不利，白粼粼接连败北，但他又不甘心，只能再战，结果还是输。

鸟气得不行，合理怀疑是宋郁把胜率给打完了。

也就在这时，白粼粼的翅膀勾住了耳机线，一不小心给扯开了，游戏对局的背景音漏了出来。

但他已经杀红了眼。

完全没有注意到身后有被子被掀开的动静，只是一个劲地输出：

“啾啾啾，煞笔队友，不许挂机！”

“啾啾，去死啊！我一大炮轰死你。”

“艹啊！”

宋郁从床上坐直了身体，头发都被压翘了，只是面色恍惚。

白粼粼最后还是眼睁睁地看着水晶被推掉了，生气极了，一爪子踹了下鼠标，砰砰跳跳地回头。

“……”

“……”

作者有话说：

[鸽子]：人，可以当没有看到吗？

Ps:鹦鹉往自己尾羽上插纸条这个，我查过，多是牡丹鹦鹉，公的母的话，好像也都有。粼粼就单纯觉得叼着费劲，他就插自己尾羽上，不用深究
