Bai Linlin, looking down from above, began to issue orders.

The human was very obedient and indeed started doing them.

chunks.chineseText:
第39章

“少年”脸都红了，他是盘着腿坐在对方的脊背上的，短裤布料堆叠在一起，露出了光洁的膝盖。

白粼粼懵住了，他的手撑的也不是地板……是宋郁的背……

滑滑的。

白粼粼身体都发烫了，他着急地就要下来，但是身下的人却轻笑了声。

然后就又做了俯卧撑。

一下，一上。

像是坐船。

好玩是好玩，但很奇怪。

白粼粼着急地要下来，甚至都开口了，慌不择路地道：

“你、你别动。”

“少年”已经试图伸着胳膊下摸索着力点了，但这个时候宋郁说话了，只是微微侧头道：

“也可以的。”

“可以坐。”

白粼粼心跳都在加速，他彻底“熟”了，一闭眼就变成了毛绒绒的小鸟，从人的身上跳了下来。

羞得啪嗒啪嗒地往门口冲。

身后还有宋郁的声音：

“粼粼？”

但鸟已经灵巧地从门缝里挤出去了，翅膀都是半伸着的，为了散热。

-

大约晚上十点钟的时候。

宋郁才结束了运动，索性直接去健身房的浴室洗了澡，他这几天都是保持这个习惯，毕竟去卧室洗，他的小鸟可能在睡觉。

少年套上了黑色的短袖，抬手拿过了手机，屏幕里泛出的光映衬着人的优越面庞，鼻梁挺直，眉骨优越。

宋郁长相偏冷，确切地来说容易给人一种不近人情的感觉，但是在他看到手机屏幕的壁纸后，眉眼都变得柔和了起来。

壁纸是一只圆滚滚的小鸟怼脸照，在歪头盯着镜头，很有精气神的样子。

他看了大约有半分钟，然后才切到了购物页面，还是一些新的零食，毕竟他的小鸟要拿去给他的朋友分享。

宋郁每周都会购入新的。

大约处理好这些，他才准备去卧室，但就在这时，手机收到了几条匿名短信：

[宋郁，你把妈妈删除了什么意思？]

[要跟我划清界限？]

[你爷爷把我的事业毁了你知道么？老爷子从前还是个明辨是非的，怎么，你去吹耳旁风了？]

宋郁站在门口，垂眸看着这些连续不断冒出来的短信，面色没有什么血色，但也很平静。

[我知道你对我有怨气……可我缺过你的零花钱吗？宋启明给你的，我少给了吗？]

宋郁有些时候也不能理解，尽管他的父母离婚许久，但似乎母亲永远活在一种比较中。

他缺钱么？

宋启明和江芮明明知道他不缺。

[不说了，反正我后天要走了，去欧洲，如果你……]

宋郁把手机关了，只是觉得面前有些黑色的物质在扭动，持续了两三秒，他才推开了门。

恢复了正常。

卧室里安安静静的，书桌上还开着灯，放着一台Iphone17proMax，宋郁走了过去摸了下温度，热热的。

他侧头看了下床上。

圆滚滚的鸟正在侧身躺着，全然装作睡熟的样子，但爪子都蜷成一团了。

宋郁本来是想走过去看看他的小鸟的，但是又担忧它觉得不自在，于是还是先出了卧室，把门关得很轻。

白粼粼松了一口气，鸟头圆滚滚的，悄咪咪地侧了下，确认人真的离开了，才一个弹跳起身，爪子在枕头上踩出来一个凹陷。

“……”

鸟有些尴尬。

鸟再次伸了伸翅膀，散热。

白粼粼其实当鸟当习惯了，会忘记自己芯子是人的事，整天当大王，不过最近学会了化形……

问题就好像出现了。

他是“人”的话，好像睡在一张床上不太合适？

也不能把人当成交通工具。

还不能大摇大摆地去浴室里找宋郁……

白粼粼莫名不爽，垂着鸟头思考，最后收了收翅膀，很生气地得出结论。

化形的弊大于利！

鸟亏了！

-

楼下茶室。

宋郁并没有打算隐瞒自己得到的消息，只是觉得应该要同爷爷说一下，同时……他自己也有些想法。

“我把江芮的微信删除了。”

少年的语气平静，最后看着唯一疼自己的老人，又问了句：

“爷爷，我这样是不对吗？”

宋峥国只是给面前的孩子倒了一杯热茶，耳清目明的，只是反问道：

“你都这么问了，你自己觉得是对是错呢？”

宋郁垂着的手指微微蜷了起来，垂着眼皮，像是想起来什么，掐了下指腹，轻声道：

“我接受了我的妈妈不爱我的事实。”

“这没什么的，我只是想斩断这个关系，这么些年了……”

宋郁突然笑了，像是有些嘲弄，又觉得自己腕骨上的疤痕有点可笑，只是道：

“他们都组建了新的家庭，步入了人生的新阶段，但我却还沉浸在过去……这不公平。”

少年只是重复：

“不公平。”

“我也要全新的生活。”

夜色安安静静的，祖孙俩最后也没有在这个话题上聊太久，而是就公司的业务和学业上谈了谈。

宋峥国其实见这孩子一点点走出来，心里还是有所欣慰的，虽然他老了，但还是能替人料理掉一些麻烦的。

“大学专业怎么选的人工智能？上次好像没有细细地问你，和爷爷讲一讲好么？”

老人面容和蔼，语气也是循循善诱的。

宋郁闻言其实怔了下。

宋峥国见状又解释了下：“你这段时间太忙了，商科那里本就不是很好读，你再兼顾这个前沿行业……孩子，我怕你累倒。”

茶室里氛围宁静，紫砂壶上还冒着一缕缕的白雾。

宋郁其实不知道怎么组织语言，因为他当时选这个，只是想实现他的小鸟的愿望。

刷爪子纹路的入户门。

“……”

不是很好说出口的样子。

“华秉是个庞大的集团，管理是最重要的部分，你以后也要担任这个领航手。关于企业发展的走向，譬如现在新兴的人工智能产业，其实你可以开辟更多岗位，成立诸多工作室，让人才发挥作用……”

宋峥国试图说得更直白：

“小郁，你不必要成为这个一线的工程师，这很累。”

宋郁其实明白这个意思，他的确课业压力很大，放弃一门专业的修读确实会减轻不少压力，但是……

他的小鸟。

“爷爷，我再考虑考虑。”

老人叹了一口气：

“你这孩子……”

-

回到卧室已经是十一点多了，鸟已安寝，手机插上了充电器，电量显示百分之五。

宋郁在书桌那里看了一会，从抽屉里拿出来一个相框，前几天物业那里送过来的，他把照片夹进去了。

是一个戴着西部牛仔帽子、身着配套的小背带、侧脸看镜头的小鸟。

写真。

宋郁前段时间带鸟去的，还自带了一些衣服，拍摄了十多套写真，花了大概有两千。

也不贵。

宋郁把这个小相框摆在了桌上，是一抬头就能看见的位置，在几个月前……这里曾是一幅家庭合影。

人总是要往前走的。

他走到了床边，看到睡熟的“少年”一点也不奇怪，最近这段时间总是这样。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 39

The "young man" was blushing. He had been sitting cross-legged on the other’s back, his shorts bunched up, revealing his smooth, clean knees.

Bai Linlin was stunned. The surface his hands were pressing against wasn't the floor... it was Song Yu’s back.

It was slippery.

Bai Linlin’s entire body felt like it was burning up. He hurriedly tried to get down, but the person beneath him let out a soft chuckle.

Then, he did another push-up.

Down, and up.

It felt like riding a boat.

It was fun, certainly, but it was also very strange.

Bai Linlin was desperate to get down, even blurting out in a panic:

"D-don't move."

The "young man" had already tried to reach out his arms to find a point of leverage, but at that moment, Song Yu spoke, turning his head slightly:

"It’s fine."

"You can sit."

Bai Linlin’s heart was racing. He was completely "cooked." With a squeeze of his eyes, he transformed into a fluffy little bird and hopped off the person’s back.

Embarrassed, he scurried toward the door, pattering along.

Behind him came Song Yu’s voice:

"Linlin?"

But the bird had already nimbly squeezed through the crack in the door, his wings half-spread to help dissipate the heat.

-

Around ten o'clock in the evening.

Song Yu finally finished his workout and decided to shower in the gym’s bathroom. He had kept this habit for the past few days; after all, if he washed in the bedroom, his little bird might be sleeping.

The young man pulled on a black short-sleeved shirt and reached for his phone. The light from the screen illuminated his superior facial features—a straight bridge of the nose and well-defined brow bones.

Song Yu’s appearance leaned toward the cold side; to be precise, it tended to give people an impression of being unapproachable. However, when he saw the wallpaper on his phone screen, his eyes softened.

The wallpaper was a close-up of a round, fluffy little bird, tilting its head and staring at the camera, looking full of spirit.

He looked at it for about half a minute before switching to a shopping page to order some new snacks. After all, his little bird needed them to share with his friends.

Song Yu bought new ones every week.

Just as he finished handling these things and prepared to head to the bedroom, his phone received a few anonymous text messages:

[Song Yu, what is the meaning of deleting Mom?]

[Are you trying to draw a line between us?]

[Do you know that your grandfather ruined my career? The old man used to be a person who could tell right from wrong. What, did you go and whisper in his ear?]

Song Yu stood at the doorway, looking down at the messages popping up one after another. His face lacked color, but he remained calm.

[I know you have a grudge against me... but have I ever been short on your allowance? Did I give you any less than what Song Qiming gave you?]

Sometimes Song Yu couldn't understand it. Even though his parents had been divorced for a long time, it seemed his mother lived in a state of constant comparison.

Was he short on money?

Song Qiming and Jiang Rui clearly knew he wasn't.

[Forget it. Anyway, I’m leaving the day after tomorrow for Europe. If you...]

Song Yu turned off his phone. He felt as if some black substance was twisting in front of him for two or three seconds before he pushed the door open.

Everything returned to normal.

The bedroom was quiet. The lamp on the desk was still on, illuminating an iPhone 17 Pro Max. Song Yu walked over and touched the surface; it was warm.

He glanced toward the bed.

The round, fluffy bird was lying on its side, pretending to be fast asleep, though its claws were curled into a ball.

Song Yu had originally wanted to walk over to check on his little bird, but he worried about making it feel uncomfortable, so he left the bedroom, closing the door very softly.

Bai Linlin let out a sigh of relief. His round bird head tilted slightly in secret. Confirming that the person had truly left, he sprang up, his claws leaving a depression in the pillow.

"..."

The bird felt a bit awkward.

He stretched his wings again to cool off.

Bai Linlin had actually become so accustomed to being a bird that he would forget he was human on the inside, acting like a little king all day. But recently, he had learned to shapeshift...

And it seemed problems had arisen.

If he was a "human," it didn't seem quite appropriate to sleep in the same bed, did it?

He couldn't treat people like a mode of transportation.

And he couldn't just swagger into the bathroom to find Song Yu...

Bai Linlin felt inexplicably annoyed. He hung his bird head in thought, finally tucking his wings in and reaching a very angry conclusion.

Shapeshifting does more harm than good!

The bird lost out!

-

Downstairs in the tea room.

Song Yu didn't intend to hide the news he had received; he just felt he should tell his grandfather, and at the same time... he had some thoughts of his own.

"I deleted Jiang Rui’s WeChat."

The young man’s tone was calm. He looked at the only elder who truly cared for him and asked:

"Grandfather, is what I did wrong?"

Song Zhengguo simply poured a cup of hot tea for the child in front of him. With clear, sharp eyes, he asked in return:

"Since you’re asking, do you think it was right or wrong yourself?"

Song Yu’s hanging fingers curled slightly. He lowered his eyelids, as if remembering something, pinched his fingertip, and said softly:

"I have accepted the fact that my mother doesn't love me."

"It’s nothing. I just want to cut off this relationship. It’s been so many years..."

Song Yu suddenly smiled, as if mocking himself. He felt the scar on his wrist was a bit ridiculous, and simply said:

"They have both started new families and entered new stages of their lives, but I am still immersed in the past... That’s not fair."

The young man repeated:

"It’s not fair."

"I want a brand-new life, too."

The night was quiet. The grandfather and grandson didn't talk about this topic for too long, instead discussing company business and studies.

Song Zhengguo was actually relieved to see the child slowly walking out of the shadows. Although he was old, he could still clear away some troubles for the boy.

"Why did you choose Artificial Intelligence for your university major? I don't think I asked you in detail last time. Tell me about it, will you?"

The old man’s face was kind, his tone coaxing.

Song Yu was actually stunned for a moment.

Seeing this, Song Zhengguo explained: "You’ve been too busy lately. Business studies are not easy to master, and you’re also taking on this cutting-edge industry... Child, I’m afraid you’ll collapse from exhaustion."

The atmosphere in the tea room was peaceful, with wisps of white steam rising from the purple clay teapot.

Song Yu didn't know how to organize his words because he had chosen it simply to fulfill his little bird’s wish.

To have a front door that could scan claw prints.

"..."

It didn't seem like something easy to say out loud.

"Huabing is a massive group, and management is the most important part. You will be the one at the helm in the future. Regarding the direction of corporate development, such as the emerging AI industry, you could actually open up more positions, establish many studios, and let talent play its role..."

Song Zhengguo tried to be more direct:

"Xiao Yu, you don't have to be an engineer on the front lines. It’s very tiring."

Song Yu understood what he meant. His academic pressure was indeed high, and dropping one major would certainly reduce the burden, but...

His little bird.

"Grandfather, let me think about it some more."

The old man sighed:

"You child..."

-

It was past eleven when he returned to the bedroom. The bird was already asleep, and the phone was plugged into the charger, showing five percent battery.

Song Yu read at the desk for a while and took a photo frame out of the drawer. It had been delivered by the property management a few days ago, and he tucked the photo inside.

It was a picture of a little bird wearing a cowboy hat and matching suspenders, looking at the camera from the side.

A portrait.

Song Yu had taken the bird to get it done a while ago. He had even brought some clothes along, taking over a dozen sets of photos, which cost about two thousand.

It wasn't expensive.

Song Yu placed the small frame on the desk, in a position where he could see it the moment he looked up. A few months ago... this spot had held a family photo.

People always have to move forward.

He walked to the bedside and saw the "young man" fast asleep. It wasn't strange anymore; it had been like that for a while now.

chunks.chineseText:
会在梦里变成“人”。

宋郁撑着手臂看了一会，潮湿的黑发盖住了些眉眼，那颗红痣若隐若现的。

“粼粼？”

鸟睡着了。

“少年”蜷着身子，睡姿一般，甚至都没有枕到枕头上。

宋郁微微弯腰，抬手托起来床上“人”的后颈，想把“人”放到枕头上，但或许是动作还是有点吵醒它了。

“少年”一个歪头，把脸埋到了他的掌心。

不动了。

像是之前把鸟头插到他的手指之间的空隙一样。

宋郁呼吸都放轻了些，眼皮微微垂着，后面才慢慢地给放到了枕头上。

不过“少年”压住他的手了。

宋郁低头看了一会，没有再挣，只是抬手拿出来了手机，翻开微信里的联系人，找出来一只头像为鹤的“人”。

发送消息道：

[您好，我是编号247粼粼的监护人，我想问一下，它总是在睡觉的时候化成人形要紧吗？]

[对它身体健康会不会有影响？]

丹顶鹤其实在管理局正加班着的，上头说是南市来了个749局的人类，让管理局这边看顾好城市里的妖怪，尽可能地低调一些……

麻烦。

丹顶鹤拿着新到手的手机刷短视频，它的饲养员给他开了个账号，现在约莫有一万粉丝了。

嗯嗯。

不过就在这时消息弹出来了，它这次看了下，越看越满意。

247的监护人是真的不错。

多有礼貌。

说得清清楚楚的。

丹顶鹤心里好感度又往上涨了涨，然后才准备回消息。

宋郁这边还在床边，单手看手机的消息，另外一个手在给“少年”当枕头。

他侧眸一直看着，直到回复来了：

[人形吗？那其实不太常见，妖怪一般睡熟会倾向于保持自己原本的形态。]

[你观察一下吧，247毕竟是走歪门邪道上来的，根基不稳也正常。]

宋郁：“……”

他不觉得是歪门邪道。

他的小鸟很努力了。

但话不能这么说，宋郁还是同丹顶鹤道了谢，不过就在这时那边又发了几条消息：

[247这些天来基地总是不务正业，组织一堆小妖怪唱歌跳舞的，你让它好好做任务，提升等级有助于它稳定妖力，它还不到一岁，正是……]

总之是一大堆话。

宋郁还是不赞同。

他的小鸟不用努力。

不过他还是回复了句：

[好的，谢谢您。]

宋郁大概就这么保持一个动作有半个小时，“少年”才转了个身子，又沉沉地睡了过去。

他的手有些麻。

但更多的是一种温软的触感。

宋郁起身这才回了床的外侧，抬手刚把卧室的灯关了，脑海里却突然又浮现丹顶鹤发的那段话。

——睡熟会倾向于保持自己原本的形态。

是么？

-

翌日。

毛绒绒的小鸡神清气爽地醒了，啪嗒啪嗒就走到人的胸膛处，开始低头注视ing。

怎么还不醒？

白粼粼刚刚看手机了，今天是周末，宋郁不需要去学校和公司，而且现在已经八点钟了。

他没睡好吗？

鸟蓬了蓬毛，最后窝在人的锁骨处了，乖巧等待。

一会要去吃早饭。

有蟹黄包的。

白粼粼已经记住了家里的一周饮食，周末是福云阁的早茶，会有人送过来的。

鸟也要吃。

宋郁其实在梦里微微蹙了蹙眉，总觉得胸口有块小石头，沉沉的，等他睁开眼的时候……

身上的小鸟已经睡起了回笼觉，鸟头插在翅根里，一个蓝色毛球。

“……”

-

早餐大约是在八点半开始的，宋峥国在楼下看报纸，见到一人一鸟下来才温声道：

“怎么今天起晚了？”

“没睡好？”

宋郁还没来得及解释，肩头的小鸟就扑棱翅膀飞了过去，端端正正地站到了餐桌上。

那里有鸟的位置。

一个小盘子，里面是草莓块和小饼干，量很少，只是给小鸟尝个鲜。

旁边还有小围兜。

是阿姨新勾的，配套的蓝色，上面还有小白花。

鸟伸喙叼了起来，啪嗒啪嗒地走到老人的跟前。

宋峥国见状也不看宋郁了，只是很认真地接了过来，抬手去细致地给鸟儿系上，夸赞道：

“好好好，有仪式感。”

白粼粼美美地开始炫饭，反正人吃完桌上的东西是不会立即收的，按照规律来说，还会放个三十分钟。

很多天都是这样。

方便了鸟。

今天他就注意到了，根本就没有人吃蟹黄包！

简直是浪费！

宋峥国年纪大了本来胃口就不是很好，吃完就拿着报纸接着看，时不时地会看一眼桌上的小鸟。

圆滚滚的。

叨一口草莓看一口桌上的食物。

贪吃的鸟儿。

宋郁也在健身，其实没有吃太多，他要保持个好的身材，他的小鸟上次提过了。

“小郁，待会同我去下书房？”

宋峥国抬了抬眼，见人吃得差不多了才问道。

“好。”

后面祖孙俩就上楼去了，鸟当然没有跟上，白粼粼甚至还特地去目送他们关上门了。

很好。

鸟啪嗒啪嗒走到蟹黄包那里，直接把短喙伸进去了，鲜美的汤汁迸发在舌尖。

毛绒绒的翅膀都伸了伸。

爪子也打了点滑。

-

书房。

“爷爷这几天要出去一趟，在琅山那里的农家乐，跟你说一声。”

宋峥国面色很是温文尔雅，对着身边的少年说道。

“几天？您身体刚恢复没多久？我陪着吧。”

宋郁蹙了蹙眉，很不放心地问。

但老人只是摆了摆手，宽慰道：

“爷爷没事，只是我那位朋友，他性格古怪，不喜旁人跟着，也是有事才来南市的。”

宋峥国又想了想：

“你要说几天？爷爷也不大清楚……大概三五天？”

宋郁其实还想再说几句，但后面都被老人不动声色地推拒了，理由很多：一是认为琅山那里的农家乐是华秉的产业，很安全；二是说明自己身体素质不错，医生也说要多多活动。

“……”

宋郁也是没办法，最后只是道：

“那您记得和我通电话。”

也就在这时，门口处传来了爪子挠动的动静，嘎吱嘎吱的，很有劲。

宋峥国笑了笑，抬手让人去开门。

鸟就这么大摇大摆地进来了，喙上其实还沾了点汤汁，非常鲜香。

宋郁见到后一愣，随即就是采取行动，捏着那个小短喙，用指腹给拭掉了。

白粼粼还以为是拔河，一个劲地往后撤，结果人一松手，他直接啪唧坐在了地板上。

鸟：？

宋郁：“……”

白粼粼很是灵巧的一个弹跳，重新站了起来，收了收翅膀，很是大大方方地进来。

鸟很有家庭成员的自觉。

他们在聊什么具体的事？

有什么是鸟不能知道的？

白粼粼扑棱翅膀飞到了桌子上，稳稳当当地站在了笔筒上，开始表态。

“鸟儿吃完了？”

鸟闻言直接僵住。

“小草莓和小饼干。”
chunks.englishText:
He would turn into a "human" in his dreams.

Song Yu propped himself up on his arms and watched for a while, his damp black hair covering his eyes, the red mole faintly visible.

"Linlin?"

The bird was asleep.

The "young man" was curled up, his sleeping posture mediocre; he wasn't even resting his head on the pillow.

Song Yu leaned over slightly and lifted the back of the "human's" neck, intending to place him on the pillow, but perhaps the movement was enough to wake him.

The "young man" tilted his head and buried his face into Song Yu’s palm.

He didn't move again.

It was just like how he used to tuck his bird head into the gaps between Song Yu’s fingers.

Song Yu’s breathing softened, his eyelids drooping slightly, before he slowly placed him onto the pillow.

However, the "young man" was pinning his hand down.

Song Yu looked down for a while and didn't pull away. He simply reached out to take his phone, opened his WeChat contacts, and found a "person" whose avatar was a crane.

He sent a message:

[Hello, I am the guardian of #247 Linlin. I would like to ask, is it a problem that it always turns into human form while sleeping?]

[Will it have any impact on its physical health?]

The Red-Crowned Crane was actually working overtime at the Management Bureau. The higher-ups said a human from the 749 Bureau had arrived in Nanshi, so the Bureau needed to keep an eye on the monsters in the city and keep things as low-key as possible...

What a nuisance.

The Red-Crowned Crane was scrolling through short videos on its new phone; its caretaker had opened an account for it, and it now had about ten thousand followers.

Mm-hmm.

Just then, the message popped up. It took a look, and the more it read, the more satisfied it felt.

#247’s guardian is truly not bad.

So polite.

And explains things so clearly.

The Red-Crowned Crane’s favorability rating rose in its heart, and it prepared to reply.

Song Yu was still by the bedside, looking at the message with one hand while the other served as a pillow for the "young man."

He kept his eyes on him until the reply came:

[Human form? That’s actually not very common. Monsters usually tend to maintain their original form when they are in a deep sleep.]

[You should observe it. After all, #247 came up through unconventional means, so it’s normal for its foundation to be unstable.]

Song Yu: "..."

He didn't think it was "unconventional means."

His little bird was very hardworking.

But he couldn't say that. Song Yu still thanked the Red-Crowned Crane. However, at that moment, the other party sent a few more messages:

[#247 has been slacking off at the base these days, organizing a bunch of little monsters to sing and dance. You should make it focus on its tasks; increasing its level will help stabilize its monster power. It’s not even a year old yet, it’s at the age where...]

In short, it was a long list of complaints.

Song Yu still didn't agree.

His little bird didn't need to work hard.

However, he still replied:

[Understood, thank you.]

Song Yu maintained that position for about half an hour before the "young man" finally turned over and fell into a deep sleep again.

His hand was a bit numb.

But more than that, he felt a warm, soft touch.

Song Yu got up and went to the outer side of the bed. Just as he reached out to turn off the bedroom light, the words the Red-Crowned Crane had sent suddenly surfaced in his mind.

—*Monsters usually tend to maintain their original form when they are in a deep sleep.*

Is that so?

-

The next day.

The fluffy little chick woke up feeling refreshed. He pattered over to the person’s chest and began to stare down at him.

Why isn't he awake yet?

Bai Linlin had just checked his phone. It was the weekend; Song Yu didn't need to go to school or the company, and it was already eight o'clock.

Didn't he sleep well?

The bird fluffed his feathers and finally nestled into the hollow of the person’s collarbone, waiting obediently.

They would have breakfast soon.

There would be crab roe buns.

Bai Linlin had already memorized the weekly diet of the house. On weekends, there was dim sum from Fuyun Pavilion, which someone would deliver.

The bird wanted to eat, too.

Song Yu was actually frowning slightly in his dream, feeling as if there was a little stone on his chest, heavy and solid. When he opened his eyes...

The little bird on his body had already gone back to sleep, his head tucked under his wing, a blue ball of fluff.

"..."

-

Breakfast started around eight-thirty. Song Zhengguo was reading the newspaper downstairs and spoke gently when he saw the person and the bird come down:

"Why did you get up late today?"

"Didn't you sleep well?"

Before Song Yu could explain, the little bird on his shoulder fluttered its wings and flew over, standing upright on the dining table.

There was a spot for the bird there.

A small plate containing strawberry chunks and small biscuits. The portion was very small, just enough for the little bird to have a taste.

Beside it was a small bib.

It was one the auntie had just crocheted, a matching blue with little white flowers on it.

The bird reached out with his beak, picked it up, and pattered over to the old man.

Seeing this, Song Zhengguo stopped looking at Song Yu and very seriously took it, raising his hand to carefully tie it on for the bird, praising:

"Good, good, good. A sense of ritual."

Bai Linlin began to feast happily. In any case, people wouldn't clear the table immediately after finishing their meal; according to the pattern, they would leave it for another thirty minutes.

It had been like that for many days.

It was convenient for the bird.

Today, he noticed that no one had even touched the crab roe buns!

What a waste!

Song Zhengguo didn't have much of an appetite due to his age, so he continued reading his newspaper after eating, glancing at the little bird on the table from time to time.

Round and chubby.

Pecking a piece of strawberry, then looking at the food on the table.

A greedy little bird.

Song Yu was also working out, so he didn't eat much; he had to maintain a good physique, as his little bird had mentioned it last time.

"Xiao Yu, come to the study with me in a while?"

Song Zhengguo raised his eyes and asked only after seeing that the person had finished eating.

"Okay."

Afterward, the grandfather and grandson went upstairs. The bird, of course, didn't follow. Bai Linlin even went out of his way to watch them close the door.

Very good.

The bird pattered over to the crab roe buns and stuck his short beak directly into one. The delicious broth burst onto the tip of his tongue.

He stretched his fluffy wings.

His claws slipped a little on the table.

-

In the study.

"I’m going out for a trip these next few days, to a farmhouse in Langshan. Just letting you know."

Song Zhengguo’s expression was very gentle as he spoke to the young man beside him.

"For how many days? Your health only just recovered. I’ll accompany you."

Song Yu frowned, asking with great concern.

But the old man just waved his hand, comforting him:

"I’m fine. It’s just that my friend has an eccentric personality and doesn't like others tagging along. He only came to Nanshi because he had business."

Song Zhengguo thought for a moment:

"How many days? I’m not quite sure... maybe three or five days?"

Song Yu actually wanted to say a few more words, but the old man deflected them all calmly. He had many reasons: first, he believed the farmhouse in Langshan was a Huabing property and very safe; second, he explained that his physical condition was good and the doctor had advised him to stay active.

"..."

Song Yu had no choice, finally saying:

"Then remember to call me."

Just then, there was a sound of claws scratching at the door, *creak, creak*, very energetic.

Song Zhengguo smiled and gestured for someone to open the door.

The bird swaggered in, his beak actually stained with a bit of broth, smelling very fresh and savory.

Song Yu was stunned when he saw this, then immediately took action, pinching that little short beak and wiping it clean with his fingertip.

Bai Linlin thought it was a tug-of-war and kept pulling back, but when the person let go, he plopped right onto the floor.

Bird: ?

Song Yu: "..."

Bai Linlin nimbly sprang up, stood back on his feet, tucked his wings in, and walked in very generously.

The bird had a strong sense of being a family member.

What specific things were they talking about?

What was it that the bird couldn't know?

Bai Linlin fluttered his wings and flew onto the desk, standing steadily on the pen holder, ready to make his presence known.

"Did the bird finish eating?"

The bird froze at the mention.

"The little strawberries and biscuits."

chunks.chineseText:
白粼粼这才定了定心，很矜持地点了点头。

宋峥国这才爽朗一笑，转而认真地道：

“爷爷要出门几天，鸟儿在家好好吃饭？”

白粼粼这才歪了歪头，要出门？

去哪里？

鸟扑棱翅膀下来了，在书桌上刚啪嗒啪嗒走几步就被宋郁给拿起来了，被迫站在了他的肩头。

少年只是认真问：

“琅山那里的工作人员知道您要去的事吗？我交代一下吧……”

“也是，我真是老了，这个都忘了。”

后面就是一些琐碎的注意事项，其实没有什么意思，白粼粼当成背景音了。

鸟专注地看书房墙上挂着的“画作”，其实原来这个地方是有一个“天道酬勤”的书法作品的，不过现在变成一幅花鸟画。

主角显而易见，是一只毛绒绒的蓝羽小鸟。

白粼粼很满意。

这个家，果然是离不开鸟的！

-

时间又推移了几天，宋峥国也抵达了琅山的一个“农家乐”。

但说是“农家乐”，其实更像是度假村，不仅风景秀丽，里面的设施也一应俱全。

“好久不见，峥国，你最近怎么样？”

对面坐着的是个道士，穿着一身八卦祥云道袍，头发也是花白，个子不高，但看着眼睛黑亮有神。

现下正拿筷子吃着牛肉片，眉眼都舒坦开了，活脱脱一个精神小老头的样子。

“我想着你这次来南市，正好问你点事……是这样。”

宋峥国犹豫了下，斟酌道：

“我有一个朋友……”

对面的人筷子一顿，抬眼看了过来，一副我看你怎么编的样子。

“……”

宋峥国没有办法，只能把事情的来龙去脉说了，但对面的小老头只是摆手道：

“你是不是看错了，或许那就是个人，不过是你孙子藏起来了，后面让人家走了而已。”

“不要封建迷信啊。”

身着道袍的人语气认真，把一盘子肉炫光了。

宋峥国只是道：“我既然撞见了，那不可能不查。”

“物业的监控我也看了，家里没有人第三人出来，房间我也一一找了，属实是没有。”

老人只是叹了口气，只是道：

“我后面看了家里近一周的监控，依然是没有，平云，我是真的只能往那里想……”

道士这才吃完，擦了擦嘴，这一路奔波的，终于投奔到宋家了。

小老头只是问：

“是让我收了它吗？”

-

宋郁后面也没有去送江芮，只是发了一句“一路顺风”，后面就把那些收到的短信全部删了。

他心情其实不是很好，以至于从学校早早地就回来了，但刚一开门，两只毛绒绒的小鸟就在挤在一起看电影，还是恐怖的那种。

宋郁进门的时候正好播放到惊悚场面，房间里响起来此起彼伏的“啾啾啾啾啾！”

很聒噪。

“……”

灰棕色小雀甚至把头放在了蓝羽小鸟的翅膀下，001觉得画面太恐怖了。

虽然它也叨过眼球之类的。

白粼粼看到宋郁回来了，熟练地用爪子踩了下鼠标，把电影给暂停了，仰头就看了过去。

“宋郁！”

少年抬步走了过去，很温和地伸了手指，鸟立即抬腿上来，一顿攀爬抵达肩头。

“打游戏打游戏。”

“001，你快过来看，学一学！”

宋郁听着自家小鸟骄傲的语气，不由得笑了下，那些负面情绪也消散了，只是照做打开了游戏。

开始操作。

肩头有两只毛绒绒的小鸟在聚精会神地看着。

-

而与此同时，琅山这里。

“那你又没有这个想法……看来这是个段位很高的妖怪了？”

道士想了想，又问：

“它是不是会蛊惑人心？”

宋峥国脑海里浮现小鸟板板正正地站着，鸟眼圆圆地看着他的样子。

“……应该？”

道士点了点头，明了，又排查：

“有没有对鲜血反应大？”

“嗜血如命吗？”

宋峥国：“……”

嗜蟹黄包如命。

-

宋郁就这么一直打到了晚上，肩头的小鸟也只剩下了一只，蓝羽小鸟困困的，后面就往他肩头挪，蓬毛，开始睡下了。

他的确不能理解。

江芮为什么认为是他吹耳边风……

他吹什么风？

他控诉什么？

宋郁还是会被影响到一些，直到怀里多了个睡着的“少年”，面对面地抱着，浅蓝色的头发甚至碰到了他的下巴，有痒痒的触感。

鸟睡着了。

又恢复成人形了。

宋郁愣了下，把游戏关了，只是抬手揽着那截腰，抱着，什么也没做。

他的小鸟特别爱美。

一天要换两套衣服，上午是走的极繁主义，身上叮叮咣咣的，戴了好多配饰；下午天气有些变冷，换成了长袖长裤，都是纯棉材质的，咖色的卫衣衬得“少年”的皮肤更白。

宋郁都是在它睡着的时候看到的，不然也不知道要换好几次。

他抬手勒了下那截腰，微微低头……

“唔。”

怀里“人”就发出这么个不舒服的气音，宋郁一夜都没有再动过了，硬生生地这么维持着抱着的姿势，让他的小鸟安眠。

-

但这样的后果就是，人生病了。

不仅仅是一夜着凉，还有前段时间连轴转，以及江芮那些匿名短信……总之是这些因素堆积到了一起。

身体开始罢工。

但就算如此，宋郁早上还是单手抱着“人”去了床上，本意是让他的小鸟再睡会儿，顺手也叫了祥云阁的早茶外送，备注了蟹黄包要新鲜的。

白粼粼其实醒过来的时候就觉得有些不对劲了，但他还是听话去吃早饭了，宋郁似乎没什么胃口，只是说要去睡一觉。

鸟有些担心。

他把美食放在一旁了，啪嗒啪嗒地在人身后跟着。

宋郁上楼也没有发现，顺手关卧室门的时候鸟从善如流地钻了进来。

之后就是躺在了床上，他昏睡了过去。

白粼粼扑棱翅膀上去了，很认真地伸着鸟头过去，抵了下。

很热。

他发烧了。

鸟担心，鸟着急。

鸟不能去打电话，因为他只是一个小鸟。

白粼粼在地板上来回转，最后没办法，只能啪嗒啪嗒地朝着洗手间那里走，用爪子打开水龙头，叼着毛巾浸湿，然后捞了出来……

毛绒绒的小鸡在地板上来回走，伸着翅膀维持平衡。

-

宋峥国提前回来了，原因是他觉得鸟儿不算什么坏妖怪，为什么要收了？

思来想去还是婉拒了朋友过来拜访的要求。

鸟儿又不会害小郁。

老人想到这里，不由得想去看看自己孙子，毕竟华秉那里说这孩子今天没来，估摸着是身体不舒服了。

宋峥国直接去了二楼的卧室那里，见门半开着，索性就抬手推开了。

也就在这时——

里面那个浅蓝色头发的少年出现了，“他”正蹲在床边，身着白色衬衫和黑色短裤，正眼巴巴地看着床上的人。

听到了门口的动静才回了头。

作者有话说：

[鸽子][鸽子]：史诗级会面！
chunks.englishText:
Bai Linlin finally steadied his heart and nodded with great reserve.

Song Zhengguo then gave a hearty laugh, turning to say earnestly:

"Grandpa is going out for a few days. Will you eat your meals well at home, little bird?"

Bai Linlin tilted his head. Going out?

Where to?

The bird fluttered down, but after taking only a few pattering steps on the desk, he was picked up by Song Yu and forced to stand on his shoulder.

The young man asked seriously:

"Do the staff at Langshan know you're coming? Should I give them a heads-up..."

"That’s true. I really am getting old; I even forgot about that."

What followed was a series of trivial instructions. It wasn't particularly interesting, so Bai Linlin treated it as background noise.

The bird focused on the "painting" hanging on the study wall. Originally, there had been a piece of calligraphy that read "Heaven Rewards Diligence," but it had since been replaced by a flower-and-bird painting.

The protagonist of the piece was clearly a fluffy little blue-feathered bird.

Bai Linlin was very satisfied.

This home, as expected, could not function without a bird!

-

A few days passed, and Song Zhengguo arrived at a "farmhouse resort" in Langshan.

Though called a "farmhouse," it was more like a vacation village; not only was the scenery beautiful, but the facilities were also fully equipped.

"Long time no see, Zhengguo. How have you been lately?"

Sitting opposite him was a Taoist priest dressed in a robe embroidered with Bagua and auspicious clouds. His hair was gray, and though he wasn't tall, his eyes were dark, bright, and spirited.

He was currently using chopsticks to eat slices of beef, his brows relaxed—the very picture of a spirited little old man.

"I was thinking that since you're in Nanshi this time, I’d take the opportunity to ask you something... It’s like this."

Song Zhengguo hesitated, choosing his words carefully:

"I have a friend who..."

The person opposite him paused his chopsticks and looked up, wearing an expression that said, *I’m waiting to see how you make this up.*

"..."

Song Zhengguo had no choice but to explain the ins and outs of the situation. However, the little old man just waved his hand:

"Did you see wrong? Perhaps it was just a person, and your grandson hid them away, then let them leave later."

"Don't be so superstitious."

The man in the Taoist robe spoke earnestly, having polished off a plate of meat.

Song Zhengguo simply replied: "Since I’ve encountered it, I cannot just leave it unchecked."

"I checked the property surveillance; no third person left the house. I searched the rooms one by one; there really was no one."

The old man sighed and said:

"I checked the home surveillance for the past week, and there was still no one. Pingyun, I really can only think in that direction..."

The Taoist finally finished eating and wiped his mouth. After the long journey, he had finally arrived at the Song residence.

The little old man asked:

"Do you want me to exorcise it?"

-

Song Yu didn't go to see Jiang Rui off later; he simply sent a text saying "Safe travels" and then deleted all the messages he had received.

He wasn't in a very good mood, so he returned home early from school. But as soon as he opened the door, two fluffy little birds were huddled together watching a movie—a horror one, at that.

When Song Yu entered, the movie was at a jump-scare scene, and the room was filled with a chorus of "Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!"

It was very noisy.

"..."

The gray-brown sparrow even tucked its head under the blue-feathered bird's wing; 001 felt the scene was too terrifying.

Even though it had pecked at eyeballs and such before.

Seeing Song Yu return, Bai Linlin skillfully used his claw to click the mouse, pausing the movie, and looked up at him.

"Song Yu!"

The young man walked over and gently extended a finger. The bird immediately stepped onto it and climbed up to his shoulder.

"Play games, play games."

"001, come over here quickly and learn!"

Hearing his little bird's proud tone, Song Yu couldn't help but smile, and his negative emotions dissipated. He simply did as asked and opened the game.

He began to play.

On his shoulder, two fluffy little birds watched with rapt attention.

-

Meanwhile, at Langshan.

"Then you don't have that feeling... It seems this is a high-level demon?"

The Taoist thought for a moment and asked:

"Does it bewitch people's hearts?"

Song Zhengguo’s mind flashed with the image of the bird standing upright and proper, its round eyes looking at him.

"...I suppose?"

The Taoist nodded, understanding, and continued his checklist:

"Does it have a strong reaction to fresh blood?"

"Is it bloodthirsty?"

Song Zhengguo: "..."

It was obsessed with crab roe buns.

-

Song Yu played until the evening. Only one little bird remained on his shoulder; the blue-feathered bird was sleepy, and eventually, it shuffled toward his shoulder, fluffed its feathers, and began to doze off.

He truly couldn't understand.

Why did Jiang Rui think he was whispering in his ear...

What wind was he blowing?

What was he accusing him of?

Song Yu was still affected by it, until he felt a sleeping "young man" in his arms, hugging him face-to-face. The light blue hair even brushed against his chin, causing a ticklish sensation.

The bird was asleep.

It had turned back into human form again.

Song Yu paused, closed the game, and simply reached out to wrap his arms around that waist, holding him, doing nothing else.

His little bird was particularly vain.

It changed outfits twice a day. In the morning, it went for maximalism, clinking and clanking with many accessories. In the afternoon, as the weather cooled, it changed into long sleeves and pants, all made of pure cotton. The brown hoodie made the "young man's" skin look even fairer.

Song Yu only saw these things when it was asleep; otherwise, he wouldn't even know it had changed so many times.

He tightened his grip on that waist and lowered his head slightly...

"Mmm."

The "person" in his arms let out an uncomfortable sound. Song Yu didn't move for the rest of the night, stubbornly maintaining the hugging posture to let his little bird sleep in peace.

-

But the consequence of this was that he fell ill.

It wasn't just catching a cold from the night; there was also the exhaustion from the recent non-stop schedule, and those anonymous texts from Jiang Rui... In short, all these factors piled up together.

His body went on strike.

Even so, in the morning, Song Yu carried the "person" to the bed with one arm, intending to let his little bird sleep a bit longer. He also ordered morning tea delivery from Xiangyun Pavilion, adding a note that the crab roe buns must be fresh.

Bai Linlin actually felt something was wrong when he woke up, but he obediently went to eat breakfast. Song Yu didn't seem to have much appetite and just said he wanted to sleep.

The bird was worried.

He left the delicacies aside and followed behind the man, pattering along.

Song Yu didn't notice as he went upstairs, and when he closed the bedroom door, the bird slipped in naturally.

After that, he lay on the bed and fell into a deep sleep.

Bai Linlin fluttered his wings and flew up, earnestly stretching his bird head over to nudge him.

He was very hot.

He had a fever.

The bird was worried; the bird was anxious.

The bird couldn't make a phone call because he was just a little bird.

Bai Linlin paced back and forth on the floor. Finally, having no other choice, he pattered toward the bathroom, used his claw to turn on the faucet, soaked a towel in his beak, and dragged it out...

The fluffy little chicken walked back and forth on the floor, stretching its wings to maintain balance.

-

Song Zhengguo returned early because he felt the bird wasn't a bad demon, so why should he exorcise it?

After thinking it over, he politely declined his friend's request to visit.

The bird wouldn't harm Xiao Yu.

Thinking of this, the old man couldn't help but want to check on his grandson. After all, Hua Bing said the boy hadn't come in today, so he guessed he might be feeling unwell.

Song Zhengguo went straight to the second-floor bedroom. Seeing the door half-open, he pushed it open.

And at that very moment—

The light blue-haired youth appeared inside. "He" was crouching by the bedside, wearing a white shirt and black shorts, looking at the person on the bed with wide, expectant eyes.

He only turned his head when he heard the movement at the door.

Author's Note:

[Pigeon][Pigeon]: An epic meeting!

chunks.chineseText: 会照顾人的一枚小鸡耶
chunks.englishText: A little chicken who knows how to take care of people.

chunks.chineseText:
第40章

时间仿佛静止了。

宋峥国纵然是再见识多，也还是不由得后退了一步，这……他没想到会这么直接撞见。

对面的“少年”也是先一愣，后面就是惶恐，猛地转过去了头，留下一个毛绒绒的后脑勺。

宋峥国想了想，当机立断走出了卧室，直接砰得一声把门给关上了。

没事，没事，只要鸟儿恢复原貌……他就当没看见。

“……”

老人也是心里砰砰跳，在门口开始踱步，脑海里不断浮现刚刚那“少年”的脸。

就巴掌大，肤色还很白。

生的……的确好看。

宋峥国想到这里愣了下，想起来一件事来，面色变得有些复杂。

原来……是只小公鸟。

-

门内的“少年”早就慌得不行了，他没有经历过这种事，一下子站了起来，几乎本能地看向床上的“人”。

想叫人。

但又想起来对方生病了。

白粼粼只好砰得一下变回小鸟，但是他看了看门口，又低着鸟头看了看自己的翅膀……

这不坐实了他是鸟变的？

不行不行。

白粼粼脑子高速运转，想起来宋郁说过的事……对象，他是对象……那爷爷是见过他的。

他有身份的！

鸟一着急，立马又幻化成人，不过这次他还没有来得及组织语言，门就又开了。

宋峥国站在门口，其实是愣了下的，这怎么……

还没变回去？

“少年”站在床边，背着手，视线都在回避，往后退了一小步，又似乎是鼓足勇气，开口想要说什么。

但就在这时——

宋峥国说了句：“鸟儿？”

白粼粼天塌了。

浅蓝色的发尾甚至都不翘了，“少年”面色都变红了，连着后退了好几步。

他被发现了。

宋峥国后知后觉自己不该这么问，但是已经晚了，面前的“少年”砰得一下化成小鸟，扑棱翅膀就飞到了床上，一个劲地往床上人的肩窝钻，毛绒绒的，爪子都在用力。

最后成功地拱到被子里了。

只留下来一点点尾羽。

没动静了。

开始装死。

“……”

宋峥国看了下卧室的情况，发现床头柜那里放着一杯热水，旁边有翻出来的退烧药，窗户开了点缝隙，保证新鲜空气的流通但不会冷到，地板也是刚拖过的，因为还有着未干的水痕……

至于床上的人，老人走过去看了下，宋郁的额头上盖着湿毛巾，拧干的那种。

“……”

或许是被窝里的某只听到了脚步声，又努力地往里拱了拱。

宋峥国看了过去，发现一点尾羽都没有了，全钻进去了。

他有些担心，这不闷么？

卧室里安安静静的。

宋峥国想了想，觉得自己吓到了它了，试着开口道：

“鸟儿？”

“你别怕。”

被窝里的凸起一开始还没有动静，后面像是被说动了，偷偷地用爪子踹开一点被子，在里面掉了个头……

很谨慎地探出鸟头。

对视ing。

宋峥国松了口气，心想可以沟通也是好的，但是刚一开口：“爷爷不是……”

嗖！

鸟头立马钻回了被子里。

速度非常之快。

再度装死。

“……”

-

宋郁是在九点半的时候清醒的，他朦朦胧胧地觉得下巴处有点痒，后面又听到一些交谈声。

“是，应该是发烧了。”

“那可能需要挂水，这样起效比较快……”

宋郁渐渐睁开了眼，视野也逐步地清晰了起来，侧了侧头，看到了房间里的情况：

家庭医生在拿着医疗包，正在调试针剂，注意到目光后才对身后的老人说：

“宋老先生，孩子醒了。”

宋郁撑着身子坐了起来，面色其实有些苍白，但是他刚想说话，肩窝的毛绒绒就开始往下滑……

他愣了下。

抬手掀开了被子。

鸟圆滚滚的，像个毛球一样窝在床单上，被发现后就啪嗒啪嗒又要往被子里面走，很是着急的样子。

宋郁抬手握住了，放到了自己肩头，侧眸问：

“怎么了？”

旁边的医生看到后抬了抬眉，说了几句：

“养了小鸟啊？”

“这么亲人。”

宋郁很温和地对医生点了下头，说道：

“是，我的小鸟。”

宋峥国抬步走了过来，视线其实是先落在孙子肩头上的小鸟的，但是对方正在专注地歪头梳理羽毛，于是只能作罢。

转而去问宋郁：

“小郁，你发烧了知道不知道？”

少年确实没办法为自己辩白，张了张口，最后只是道：

“我想着睡一觉就好了。”

“不过爷爷你怎么这么早回来了？”

宋郁其实并没有发现什么异常，他还是照旧地同自己爷爷沟通，顺带伸出去了手背，血管处有轻微的刺痛，粗针扎了进去，有微凉的液体输入。

“我那老友他后面说有事，已经来市区了，所以就不待在琅山那里了。”

宋峥国说完这话，背着手在卧室里来回走动着，虽说是看着吊瓶的液体容量，但实际上目光一直在偷偷看鸟。

“爷爷？”

宋峥国闻言立马站直了身子，咳嗽了两声，摆了摆手说“没事”。

但少年不这么觉得，他说完那话就侧头看了下肩头的那只，鸟已经梳理羽毛有十几分钟了。

“……”

怎么了？

-

与此同时，管理局内。

丹顶鹤这次选择了非常优雅的藏蓝色丝带，在“工作室”内调整了一下位置，又询问了下旁边的杜宾：

“怎么样，可以吧？”

兽头人身的杜宾点了点头，又看了看手表的时间，提醒道：

“时间差不多了。”

丹顶鹤推开了“工作室”的门，以它为首，两侧有着一堆各色各样的妖怪，虽然都保持着一些人类的装扮，但都留有自己本体的特征。

它们具有化形的能力，但更以自己的物种自豪。

先是优雅从容的狸花猫，伸着自己的美甲细细品味；后面是一只戴着墨镜的眼镜王蛇，很从容地半直立爬行；最后则是一只戴着蝴蝶结发箍的角蛙，在后面蹦蹦跳跳的……

这些都是窗口的负责人。

由于丹顶鹤能说会道，所以被派为代表，而大厅的正前方，有一扇门打开了，一队西服革履的鼠鼠也严阵以待，请过来了后面的人。

一个穿着道袍的老头子。

对视。

丹顶鹤很是优雅地伸了下翅膀，平和地道：

“请。”

城市毕竟是人类建立起来的，妖怪管理局处在人流密集处，且近年化形的妖怪数量剧增，其实是有些反常的。

灵气涌动得太频繁了。

749局关注到了这个现象，并且开始定期派遣专员来地方视察，主要是来妖怪管理局查看登记在册的档案。

一来判断妖怪数量，二来看管理局是否尽职。

而面前这个道士，就是今年749局的“专员”。

丹顶鹤它们带着这个人类去了“会议室”，那是个长长的桌子，背景上有金纹流动，很是富丽堂皇。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 40

Time seemed to stand still.

Even with all his experience, Song Zhengguo couldn't help but take a step back. This... he hadn't expected to run into it so directly.

The "youth" opposite him was also stunned for a moment, then panicked, abruptly turning his head away and leaving only a fluffy back of his head.

Song Zhengguo thought for a moment and decisively walked out of the bedroom, slamming the door shut with a bang.

It’s fine, it’s fine. As long as the bird turns back... he would just pretend he hadn't seen anything.

"..."

The old man’s heart was pounding as he began to pace at the door, the face of that "youth" constantly flashing in his mind.

It was only the size of a palm, and the skin was so fair.

He was... indeed good-looking.

Song Zhengguo paused as he thought of this, remembering something, and his expression became complicated.

So... it was a little male bird.

-

The "youth" inside the door was already panicking. He had never experienced such a thing. He stood up abruptly, almost instinctively looking at the "person" on the bed.

He wanted to call out to him.

But then he remembered the other was sick.

Bai Linlin had no choice but to turn back into a little bird with a *poof*. But he looked at the door, then lowered his bird head to look at his own wings...

Wouldn't this confirm that he was a bird in disguise?

No, no.

Bai Linlin's brain worked at high speed. He remembered what Song Yu had said... partner, he was his partner... and Grandpa had seen him before.

He had an identity!

In his anxiety, the bird immediately transformed back into a human. But this time, before he could organize his words, the door opened again.

Song Zhengguo stood at the door, actually stunned for a moment. Why...

Hadn't he turned back yet?

The "youth" stood by the bedside, hands behind his back, avoiding eye contact. He took a small step back, seemingly gathering his courage, and opened his mouth as if to say something.

But at that moment—

Song Zhengguo said: "Little bird?"

Bai Linlin's world collapsed.

The light blue tips of his hair stopped curling. The "youth's" face turned red, and he retreated several steps.

He had been discovered.

Song Zhengguo realized too late that he shouldn't have asked that, but it was already too late. The "youth" in front of him turned into a little bird with a *poof*, fluttered his wings, and flew onto the bed, burrowing desperately into the crook of the sick man's shoulder. He was all fluffy, his claws digging in with effort.

Finally, he successfully burrowed under the quilt.

Only a tiny bit of tail feather remained.

There was no movement.

He started playing dead.

"..."

Song Zhengguo looked at the situation in the bedroom. He saw a cup of hot water on the nightstand, fever-reducing medicine that had been taken out, the window left slightly ajar to ensure fresh air circulation without letting in the cold, and the floor had just been mopped, as there were still damp water marks...

As for the person on the bed, the old man walked over to check. Song Yu’s forehead was covered with a wet towel, one that had been wrung out.

"..."

Perhaps the one under the covers heard footsteps and tried to burrow even deeper.

Song Zhengguo looked over and found that not even a tail feather was left; it had all gone inside.

He was a bit worried. Wouldn't it be stuffy?

The bedroom was quiet.

Song Zhengguo thought for a moment, feeling he had scared it, and tried to speak:

"Little bird?"

"Don't be afraid."

The bulge under the quilt didn't move at first, but later, as if persuaded, it cautiously kicked the quilt open a little, turned around inside...

And very cautiously poked its bird head out.

Staring contest.

Song Zhengguo breathed a sigh of relief, thinking that being able to communicate was a good thing. But just as he opened his mouth: "Grandpa isn't..."

*Whoosh!*

The bird head immediately dove back under the quilt.

The speed was incredibly fast.

Playing dead again.

"..."

-

Song Yu woke up at 9:30. He felt a bit of an itch on his chin in his hazy state, and later heard some conversation.

"Yes, it should be a fever."

"Then he might need an IV drip; that will be more effective..."

Song Yu gradually opened his eyes, his vision slowly clearing. He tilted his head and saw the situation in the room:

The family doctor was holding a medical kit, adjusting the injection. Noticing his gaze, he said to the old man behind him:

"Mr. Song, the child is awake."

Song Yu propped himself up to sit, his face looking quite pale. But just as he wanted to speak, the fluffy thing in the crook of his shoulder began to slide down...

He was stunned.

He reached out and lifted the quilt.

The bird was round and plump, curled up on the sheets like a fur ball. Once discovered, it pattered and tried to walk back under the quilt, looking very anxious.

Song Yu reached out, held it, and placed it on his shoulder, tilting his head to ask:

"What's wrong?"

The doctor nearby raised an eyebrow when he saw this and said:

"You keep a little bird?"

"It's so affectionate."

Song Yu nodded gently to the doctor and said:

"Yes, my little bird."

Song Zhengguo walked over. His gaze had actually fallen on the little bird on his grandson's shoulder first, but since the bird was focused on tilting its head to preen its feathers, he had to give up.

He turned to ask Song Yu:

"Xiao Yu, did you know you had a fever?"

The young man really couldn't defend himself. He opened his mouth, but in the end, he only said:

"I thought I'd be fine after a sleep."

"But Grandpa, why did you come back so early?"

Song Yu didn't actually notice anything unusual. He communicated with his grandfather as usual, while extending the back of his hand. There was a slight stinging sensation at the vein as the thick needle was inserted, and cool liquid began to flow in.

"My old friend said he had something to do and had already come to the city, so I didn't stay in Langshan."

After saying this, Song Zhengguo paced back and forth in the bedroom with his hands behind his back. Although he was looking at the volume of the IV drip, his eyes were actually secretly watching the bird.

"Grandpa?"

Hearing this, Song Zhengguo immediately stood straight, coughed twice, and waved his hand, saying "It's nothing."

But the young man didn't think so. After saying that, he turned his head to look at the one on his shoulder. The bird had been preening its feathers for over ten minutes.

"..."

What was wrong?

-

Meanwhile, at the Bureau.

The Red-crowned Crane chose a very elegant navy blue ribbon this time, adjusted its position in the "studio," and asked the Doberman next to it:

"How is it? Is this okay?"

The Doberman, with the head of a beast and the body of a human, nodded and checked the time on his watch, reminding:

"It's about time."

The Red-crowned Crane pushed open the door to the "studio." Led by it, a group of various demons followed on both sides. Although they all maintained some human attire, they all retained features of their original forms.

They had the ability to shapeshift, but they took more pride in their own species.

First was an elegant and composed Tabby Cat, stretching its manicured nails to admire them; behind it was a King Cobra wearing sunglasses, crawling along in a composed, semi-upright posture; and finally, a Horned Frog wearing a bow headband, hopping along behind...

These were the heads of the various service windows.

Because the Red-crowned Crane was eloquent, it was sent as the representative. At the front of the hall, a door opened, and a team of mice in suits stood at attention, ushering in the person behind them.

An old man wearing a Taoist robe.

They locked eyes.

The Red-crowned Crane extended its wing elegantly and said peacefully:

"Please."

After all, the city was built by humans. The Demon Management Bureau was located in a densely populated area, and the number of shapeshifting demons had increased rapidly in recent years, which was actually somewhat abnormal.

The spiritual energy was surging too frequently.

Bureau 749 had noticed this phenomenon and began to regularly dispatch specialists to local areas, mainly to check the registered files at the Demon Management Bureau.

One purpose was to determine the number of demons, and the other was to see if the Bureau was doing its job.

And the Taoist in front of them was this year's "specialist" from Bureau 749.

The Red-crowned Crane and the others led the human to the "conference room." It was a long table with gold patterns flowing in the background, looking quite magnificent.

chunks.chineseText:
道士老头看了下自己的手机，果不其然没有信号，这里的“界”是由妖怪们控制的。

749局虽然名义上可以“视察”，但妖怪管理局也做出了规定，只允许单独的人类进入基地。

算是一种微妙的抗衡。

“为什么现在妖怪的数量越来越多了？”

道士声音中气十足的，环着手臂就是质问，他是真的觉得有问题。

妖界还研发出了什么津贴制……那是怎么弄出来的？

丹顶鹤不卑不亢地道：

“灵气复苏而已，少见多怪。”

道士：“……”

“那大量妖怪聚集在城市，本来就很不合理，妖怪就应该回归山林！”

丹顶鹤闻言很是生气，直接伸翅膀拍桌子了，义正词严地道：

“什么叫回归山林？世界只是你们人类的世界吗？山林……山林不全被你们砍伐了吗？”

“我们很多同族都无家可归！”

道士这次做了充足的准备，从包里拿出来相关的文件说明，一把拍了过去：

“请看！”

“我国植树造林全球领先，我国推动野生动物繁衍生存也是逐步推进，这些都是有数据的！”

丹顶鹤：“……”

谁不会？

丹顶鹤也从杜宾手里拿出来了一沓文件，义正词严地道：

“请看！”

“我国搜救犬、导盲犬、缉毒犬数量连攀新高，它们终身都在为拯救人类而奋斗！”

道士愣了下，刚想说话。

丹顶鹤又拿出一沓：

“再看！”

“全国文旅行业新兴，动物园是一大的趋势，我们的同族兢兢业业地上班，为人类创收做出了贡献！”

道士眉心一跳，果不其然对面还有牌。

丹顶鹤从容再次伸出翅膀，桌子尽头那里有一队西服革履的小鼠，顶着文件就过来了。

“还有！”

“现在网络媒体发达！在经济下行的情况下，有诸多宠物博主走上风口，我们的同族为它们主人带来了收入，为整个人类群体都提供了就业岗位！”

“还有各种宠物交易场所，狗咖、猫咖……我们还提供了情绪价值！”

“天知道你们人类有多脆弱！”

“就这还把我们赶到山林里去？”

道士：“……”

-

与此同时，锦园。

宋郁输完液已经是十点多了，他情况还不是很好，昏昏沉沉的，手背上的针已经拔掉了。

家庭医生留下来些药物，之后就先离开了，宋峥国下楼去送客了。

卧室此刻只有一人一鸟。

宋郁没有想到今天会这么严重，他还是有些反胃，面色都很苍白。

只是伸着手，他的小鸟就在他的掌心。

“粼粼不开心？”

“早饭也没吃多少。”

少年唇角微微向上抿了下，很温和地开口问。

“告诉我。”

白粼粼闻言还愣了下，本来他是低着鸟头用爪子刨宋郁的手，打算自己先emo一会儿，毕竟人生病了，他一说对方肯定又要处理事情。

但是现在……

鸟歪头看向人。

宋郁眼眸微垂着，重复道：

“告诉我，发生了什么？”

白粼粼其实有点心动了，爪子都往前伸了一步，他就是很郁闷，被发现了……

鸟侧了下头，看门那里没什么动静，索性就化形了。

宋郁唇角微微上扬，面前多了个跨坐在他身上的“少年”，他抬手就揽住对方的腰。

侧头看着，等着“人”讲。

“我今天早上……”

嘎吱——

门开了。

宋郁掌心的温度立马消逝，被子上多了个毛绒绒的小鸡，啪嗒啪嗒地往他的方向走，一个鸟头扎进被子里，拱了拱，再次进去了。

少年微微蹙了下眉，侧眸看向门口，看到是宋峥国后才眉眼平和了起来。

“爷爷。”

老人走了过来，很关心地问：“好点了没有？”

宋郁闻言点了点头，“我没事，没有那么头晕了，您放心。”

卧室里安安静静的。

就这么过了几秒钟。

宋峥国深吸一口气，仿佛是实在忍不住了，环顾了下四周，问：

“鸟儿呢？”

宋郁其实是怔了下，甚至自动回答：

“它在睡觉。”

被子里的凸起动了下。

宋峥国：“……”

“您找它有什么事吗？”

眼看着孙子看得这么紧，宋峥国一时半会还没办法，但他其实就想和鸟儿谈一谈，并没有恶意的。

老人叹了口气，他现在也不想同孩子说他知道这事，生病了，起码是要休息一下午才行。

不过就在这时，宋峥国像是突然想起来什么，转头很和蔼地道：

“祥云阁的蟹黄包又送过来新的了，我想着鸟儿估计喜欢，它来尝尝？”

宋郁眉心一跳：

“有盐，它不能……”

被子的凸起往上顶了下。

“……”

宋峥国又道：“我想起来了，前些天你奶奶托梦，说我给了鸟儿见面礼，她也不能落人于后。”

“她早年就爱买金子，还有一套小金猪，不知道鸟儿喜欢不喜欢。”

被子的凸起顶得更高了。

“噢对了，小郁你请的那位阿姨早上又送过来一个盒子，我看里头全是些小衣服，有个还是小夹克呢……”

被子终于被顶开了。

一个毛绒绒鸟头探了出来，歪头看着老人。

鸟眼圆圆的。

真的？

宋郁：“……”

“你要去吗？困不困？”

“困可以睡觉的。”

宋郁神色平静，只是低头询问，用手指碰了碰小鸟的羽毛。

“啾啾！”

鸟啪嗒啪嗒地出来了，站到了床边，仰头看着老人。

宋郁面色沉了下来。

-

管理局这里还是在吵。

“可这里是城市，人员本就密集，除了南市本地的居民之外，还有广泛的外来务工人员，负责社会治安的相关部门压力已经很大了。再出现大量的妖怪，必然是会乱套的！”

道士仍然是坚持地站在人类的立场上，他确实是749局的激进派，妖怪这种生灵应当与人类保持距离，而不是混杂在一起。

这么不起眼的一个小巷……人来人往的。

但凡有个妖怪起了邪念，想要快速提升修为，那会不会直接吞食路边的人？

那是多大的安全隐患！

丹顶鹤也很生气，伸着翅膀就怒斥：

“什么意思？妖怪多了就乱套？时代变了好不好！你以为你们人类肉质很好吗？”

“那些攻击人类的妖怪，你去灰榜上看看，哪个不是深山老林的，它们那是纯粹没吃的。”

“城市里多的是好吃的，串串香，麻辣烫，烤冷面！我们妖怪有东西吃！”

“真给自己贴脸，城市的人类天天通勤加班，皮肉早就垮了！谁要吃！”

桌子上的小妖怪都纷纷附和，有几只还窃窃私语道：

“这个专员一看就不注重保养。”

“像个枯树。”

“就是就是！”

道士闭了闭眼，彻底没招了，不过他深吸一口气，还是问：

“你能够确切地保证城市的妖怪绝对不会攻击人类吗？”
chunks.englishText:
The old Taoist priest checked his phone; as expected, there was no signal. The "realm" here was controlled by the yokai.

Although the 749 Bureau nominally had the right to "inspect," the Yokai Management Bureau had established regulations allowing only individual humans to enter their base.

It was a delicate sort of standoff.

"Why is the number of yokai increasing so rapidly?"

The Taoist’s voice was full of vigor. He crossed his arms and demanded an answer; he truly felt there was something wrong.

The Yokai Realm had even developed some kind of subsidy system... how did they even manage that?

The Red-Crowned Crane remained composed and replied:

"It’s just the resurgence of spiritual energy. Don't be so surprised by the mundane."

The Taoist: "..."

"The fact that a large number of yokai are gathering in the city is inherently unreasonable. Yokai should return to the mountains and forests!"

The Red-Crowned Crane was quite indignant at this. It slammed its wing onto the table and retorted righteously:

"What do you mean 'return to the mountains'? Is the world only for you humans? The mountains... haven't they all been logged by you?"

"Many of our kin are homeless!"

The Taoist had come well-prepared. He pulled relevant documents from his bag and slapped them onto the table:

"Look at this!"

"Our country leads the world in afforestation, and we are gradually promoting the propagation and survival of wild animals. These are all backed by data!"

The Red-Crowned Crane: "..."

Who couldn't do that?

The Red-Crowned Crane took a stack of documents from a Doberman and retorted righteously:

"Look at this!"

"The number of search-and-rescue dogs, guide dogs, and drug-sniffing dogs in our country is hitting new highs. They spend their entire lives striving to save humans!"

The Taoist paused, just about to speak.

The Red-Crowned Crane pulled out another stack:

"Look again!"

"The national cultural tourism industry is booming, and zoos are a major trend. Our kin are working diligently, contributing to human revenue!"

The Taoist’s brow twitched; as expected, the other side had more cards to play.

The Red-Crowned Crane calmly extended its wing again. At the end of the table, a team of mice in suits and leather shoes scurried over, carrying documents.

"And there's more!"

"Network media is highly developed now! In an economic downturn, many pet bloggers have ridden the trend. Our kin have brought income to their owners and provided jobs for the entire human population!"

"There are also various pet trading venues, dog cafes, cat cafes... we provide emotional value!"

"Heaven knows how fragile you humans are!"

"And you still want to drive us back into the mountains?"

The Taoist: "..."

-

Meanwhile, at Jinyuan.

It was past ten o'clock when Song Yu finished his IV drip. His condition was still not great; he felt dizzy and lethargic, and the needle had already been removed from the back of his hand.

The family doctor left some medication and departed. Song Zheng-guo went downstairs to see him off.

In the bedroom, there was only one person and one bird.

Song Yu hadn't expected things to be this serious today. He still felt nauseous, and his complexion was pale.

He simply extended his hand, and his little bird rested in his palm.

"Is Linlin unhappy?"

"You didn't eat much breakfast either."

The young man’s lips curled slightly upward as he asked gently.

"Tell me."

Bai Linlin was stunned by the words. Originally, he had been bowing his head, using his claws to scratch Song Yu’s hand, intending to wallow in his own misery for a while—after all, the human was sick, and if he spoke, the human would surely try to handle things.

But now...

The bird tilted its head to look at the human.

Song Yu’s eyes were slightly lowered as he repeated:

"Tell me, what happened?"

Bai Linlin was actually tempted; he had even moved a claw forward. He was just feeling very depressed, and now that he’d been found out...

The bird tilted its head, checked that there was no movement at the door, and simply transformed.

Song Yu’s lips curved upward. A "young man" was now straddling his lap. He reached out and wrapped his arms around the other’s waist.

He tilted his head, waiting for the "person" to speak.

"This morning, I..."

*Creak—*

The door opened.

The warmth in Song Yu’s palm vanished instantly. A fluffy little chick appeared on the quilt, pattering toward him. It buried its head into the bedding, burrowed around, and disappeared inside.

The young man frowned slightly and glanced toward the door. His expression softened only when he saw it was Song Zheng-guo.

"Grandfather."

The old man walked over and asked with concern: "Are you feeling better?"

Song Yu nodded. "I'm fine. I'm not as dizzy anymore. Don't worry."

The bedroom was quiet.

A few seconds passed.

Song Zheng-guo took a deep breath, as if he couldn't help himself. He looked around the room and asked:

"Where is the bird?"

Song Yu was actually stunned for a moment, even answering automatically:

"It's sleeping."

The lump under the quilt moved.

Song Zheng-guo: "..."

"Is there something you need from it?"

Seeing how tightly his grandson was guarding it, Song Zheng-guo couldn't do much for the moment, but he really just wanted to talk to the bird; he meant no harm.

The old man sighed. He didn't want to tell the child that he knew about this yet. Since he was sick, he needed at least an afternoon of rest.

However, just then, Song Zheng-guo seemed to remember something. He turned and said kindly:

"The Xiangyun Pavilion sent over some new crab roe buns. I thought the bird might like them. Should it come and have a taste?"

Song Yu’s brow twitched:

"They contain salt, it can't..."

The lump under the quilt poked upward.

"..."

Song Zheng-guo added: "I remembered that your grandmother mentioned in a dream the other day that I gave the bird a welcoming gift, and she couldn't be outdone."

"She loved buying gold in her younger years, and there's a set of little gold pigs. I wonder if the bird would like them."

The lump under the quilt poked up even higher.

"Oh, right, Xiao Yu, that lady you hired sent over another box this morning. I looked inside and it was full of little clothes, there's even a little jacket..."

The quilt was finally pushed aside.

A fluffy bird head poked out, tilting to look at the old man.

The bird's eyes were round.

*Really?*

Song Yu: "..."

"Do you want to go? Are you sleepy?"

"You can sleep if you're tired."

Song Yu’s expression was calm as he looked down, touching the little bird’s feathers with his finger.

"Chirp chirp!"

The bird hopped out, stood at the edge of the bed, and looked up at the old man.

Song Yu’s expression darkened.

-

Back at the Bureau, the argument continued.

"But this is a city! It’s densely populated. Aside from the local residents of Nanshi, there are vast numbers of migrant workers, and the departments responsible for public security are already under immense pressure. If a large number of yokai appear, it will inevitably lead to chaos!"

The Taoist still insisted on the human perspective. He was indeed a radical of the 749 Bureau; he believed that creatures like yokai should keep their distance from humans, not mingle with them.

Such an inconspicuous little alley... people coming and going.

If any yokai harbored evil intentions and wanted to quickly increase their cultivation, wouldn't they just devour the people on the street?

What a massive safety hazard!

The Red-Crowned Crane was also angry, extending its wings to scold him:

"What do you mean? Chaos just because there are more yokai? The times have changed, alright! Do you think you humans taste that good?"

"Those yokai that attack humans—go check the Gray List. Which one of them isn't from the deep mountains and forests? They’re just purely hungry."

"There are plenty of delicious things in the city! Skewers, spicy hot pot, grilled cold noodles! We yokai have food to eat!"

"Don't flatter yourselves! The humans in the city commute and work overtime every day; their skin and flesh have long since gone slack! Who would want to eat that!"

The little yokai on the table chimed in, and a few whispered:

"This commissioner clearly doesn't pay attention to skincare."

"Looks like a withered tree."

"Exactly, exactly!"

The Taoist closed his eyes, completely at a loss. But he took a deep breath and asked:

"Can you definitively guarantee that the yokai in the city will never attack humans?"

chunks.chineseText:
丹顶鹤觉得这简直就是在侮辱它们，很认真地道：

“城市里的妖怪，绝大多数是小型的，它们有的从出生起就是待在它们的监护人身边的，最早接触的不是人类的恶意，而是那种全然的照顾和爱。”

“我们怎么可能去攻击监护人的同族？”

道士愣了下。

丹顶鹤直接起身了，伸着翅膀就示意这个“专员”跟他来，很快它们就抵达了大厅东南角的“历史回廊”。

“中央一开始就给我们下了指示，说要强化历史教育，妖怪和人的相处时间本就很长，从古至今都有纷争，好不容易现在出现了稳定的局面，我们一定要维持好。”

“所以你看，我们还修建了纪念墙。”

丹顶鹤很是从容自信地介绍道，还伸翅膀指了指照片下面的注释，很专业地道：

“这里有照片的信息，南市管理局成立于九十年代，那个时候还很没有组织……”

道士在后面看着，说不震惊是假的，他没有想到这群妖怪居然弄得像模像样的，这学了不少人类的吧？

老头微微后仰，面色其实已经有了欣赏之意。

成。

还不错。

但就在这时。

丹顶鹤指着一幅巨大的红底合影道：

“你看，这是我们首位监护人亲自前来为他的小鸟注册登记，这实在是具有历史意义的一幕！”

“像这样的人类，我们妖界是非常欢迎的！”

道士抬眼看了过去，一秒，两秒……

他僵住了。

这不是，峥国的孙子吗？

旁边……是只巨鸟？

-

鸟这会儿已经高高兴兴地跟着老人出来了，啪嗒啪嗒地在地板上走着。

白粼粼其实已经衡量过了，既然瞒不下去了，那就不瞒了，反正宋郁那个时候他就装不下去。

说不准……

宋郁接受度高是继承了爷爷？

鸟在后面走着，用翅膀托了下鸟头，沉思。

不过也没有关系。

宋郁肯定站在他这一边的！

鸟又鼓起了信心，大摇大摆地跟在后面。

书房里鲜香四溢。

宋峥国说到做到，出高价半路截胡了祥云阁的外送，蟹黄包还冒着热气。

与此同时，他也从三楼储藏室拿下来一个黑匣子，打开了，里面是一个圆滚滚的金猪。

至于楼下那套小衣服，当然也是带了上来，很时尚的小夹克，阿姨还做了内衬的。

白粼粼一开始还吃得很开心，后面就有点默默心虚了，伸爪子后退了几步。

真奇怪，不确定真假的时候，希望是真的。

但确定都是实打实的之后，他又有点退缩。

“鸟儿，我没有恶意。”

宋峥国很诚恳地道。

“小郁这孩子，其实没有得到过太多的爱，他父母不尽责，我也何尝不是？我工作繁忙，即使是带着他，也很难抽出来时间去陪伴。”

“他自己在空旷的房子里住了很久。”

老人不知道怎么解释，他只是道：

“谢谢你，鸟儿。”

白粼粼爪子并了并，其实觉得有点不敢当，他自从来了宋家，吃得珠圆玉润的。

当鸟当得忘我了。

很爽的。

但对面的老人还在继续，面容都很宽和，只是娓娓道来一件事：

“爷爷以前从军的时候，遇见一件事，那个时候是冬天，东北的雪厚得到膝盖，当时啊，条件艰苦，没有那么多的棉衣，人都冻得麻木，脚步也不自觉地慢了下来……”

“但这其实很危险的，我掉队了，冰天雪地的，白茫茫一片，天色也暗了，只有那黑色的松林……”

白粼粼听得有些入神，啪嗒啪嗒地走了过去，仰头看着老人。

“啾啾！”

[然后呢？]

宋峥国闻言笑了下，回想起来那段奇妙的经历，只是道：

“有一头鹿走了过来，它的角是泛着金光的，我几乎没了知觉，但是它一靠近……周身却暖和了起来。”

“后面意识都变得模糊不清了，隐约觉得是一位男童，在牵着我的手走……直到我再醒过来，身边就已经围着我的战友了……”

白粼粼觉得好神奇，居然还会引路，他也忘了自己也是妖怪这件事了，只是仰头又催促道：

“啾啾！”

[继续继续！]

宋峥国的语气变得很平和，“同战友们讲他们是不信的，因为在他们的眼里，我是自己走过来的。”

“后来我去当地的猎户那里问过，他们管这种生灵叫做……”

“山神。”

-

管理局内。

丹顶鹤本来相当骄傲地介绍了这副图片，但是那位“专员”似乎大为震惊，只是反复地向它确认247的监护人姓名。

它只能指了指照片下面。

这不是写着么？

[宋郁]

道士闭了闭眼，不愿面对现实，后面老头只是伸出来一根手指，提要求道：

“我需要查一下这个妖怪的档案。”

丹顶鹤虽然有些不解，但还是很有自信的，查就查！

它们管理局的每一个妖怪都是好的！

不过就在这时，身后传来一句悠悠的叹息：

“究竟是谁教你们这么拍照的……还是红底……”

-

后面查档的时候其实是有点不顺利的，因为道士提出了一点疑问：

“它在七月的时候，妖力登记还是F级。”

“怎么八月末就直接到A级？这合规吗？”

丹顶鹤：“……”

它就知道247迟早会给它闯出祸事来。

走歪门邪道。

“是不是吃人了！”

道士表情很是严肃，觉得相当有问题，尤其是这只妖怪，应该……还在老友的家里。

丹顶鹤闭了闭眼，只是解释道：

“不是，它一个F级的鸟，啃人的手指都费劲，这是它用其他妖怪的妖力津贴快速提上去的……”

道士这下可算找到问题了，直接质问：

“妖力津贴不是只能一妖一用吗？这怎么还可以叠加使用？”

“绝对有问题！”

“这个编号247的，必须要转移至749局检查。”

丹顶鹤这就怒了，一翅膀拍桌子，道：

“你摆什么谱！”

“它没有问题就是没有问题！不信我就跟你一起去，它现在也就八个月大，一岁还不到，能吃你的手指头啊！”

道士正有此意：

“去就去！”

-

锦园这里一片祥和。

白粼粼后面试探着化形了，站在书房里，面色有些茫然，后面只是道：

“我其实什么也不会。”

“现在只学会了化形。”

宋峥国笑着道：

“叫我爷爷就好。”

鸟不好意思，背了背手。

“这样的话，那倒是的确可以给鸟儿买金镯子了。”

白粼粼垂着头，面色有些泛红，挺不好意思的，他也就展示了一会儿，立马又变成一只圆滚滚的小鸟。

不过就在这时，楼下有急促的拍门声。

宋峥国蹙了蹙眉，起身准备去看看情况，鸟也没别的事，扑棱翅膀站到人的肩膀上了。

大约一分钟后。

打开了玄关的大门。
chunks.englishText:
The Red-Crowned Crane felt this was an absolute insult to them and said very seriously:

"The vast majority of yokai in the city are small. Some have stayed by their guardians' sides since birth. The first thing they encountered wasn't human malice, but total care and love."

"How could we possibly attack the kin of our guardians?"

The Taoist was stunned.

The Red-Crowned Crane stood up and gestured with its wing for this "commissioner" to follow. They soon arrived at the "Corridor of History" in the southeast corner of the hall.

"The central office gave us instructions from the start to strengthen historical education. The time yokai and humans have spent together is very long, and there have been disputes from ancient times to the present. Now that we have finally achieved a stable situation, we must maintain it well."

"So look, we even built a memorial wall."

The Red-Crowned Crane introduced it with calm confidence, pointing its wing at the notes under the photos, speaking very professionally:

"Here is the information for the photos. The Nanshi Bureau was established in the nineties. Back then, it was still very unorganized..."

The Taoist watched from behind, and it would be a lie to say he wasn't shocked. He hadn't expected this group of yokai to have set things up so properly. They must have learned quite a bit from humans, right?

The old man leaned back slightly, his expression showing a hint of appreciation.

Not bad.

Actually quite good.

But just then.

The Red-Crowned Crane pointed to a huge group photo with a red background and said:

"Look, this is our first guardian coming in person to register his little bird. This is truly a moment of historical significance!"

"The Yokai Realm is very welcoming to humans like this!"

The Taoist looked over. One second, two seconds...

He froze.

Isn't this... Zheng-guo’s grandson?

And next to him... is a giant bird?

-

The bird was already happily following the old man out, pattering along the floor.

Bai Linlin had actually weighed the situation. Since he couldn't hide it anymore, he wouldn't. Besides, he hadn't been able to keep up the act when Song Yu was around anyway.

Perhaps...

Song Yu’s high acceptance was inherited from his grandfather?

The bird walked behind, supporting its head with a wing, deep in thought.

But it didn't matter.

Song Yu would definitely be on his side!

The bird regained its confidence and strutted along behind.

The study was filled with a fresh, savory aroma.

Song Zheng-guo kept his word. He had paid a high price to intercept the delivery from Xiangyun Pavilion mid-way, and the crab roe buns were still steaming.

At the same time, he had brought down a black box from the third-floor storage room. He opened it to reveal a round, golden pig.

As for the little clothes downstairs, he had naturally brought those up too—a very stylish little jacket, and the lady had even added a lining.

Bai Linlin had eaten happily at first, but later he felt a bit guilty and took a few steps back with his claws.

It was strange. When he wasn't sure if things were real, he hoped they were.

But now that he knew they were solid, real items, he felt a bit of hesitation.

"Bird, I mean no harm."

Song Zheng-guo said very sincerely.

"Xiao Yu, this child, hasn't actually received much love. His parents were irresponsible, and haven't I been the same? My work was busy, and even when I had him with me, it was hard to find time to keep him company."

"He lived in that empty house by himself for a long time."

The old man didn't know how to explain it, he just said:

"Thank you, bird."

Bai Linlin brought his claws together. He actually felt he didn't deserve it. Since coming to the Song family, he had been eating until he was plump and round.

He had been enjoying being a bird a bit too much.

It was great.

But the old man opposite him continued, his face gentle as he recounted a story:

"When I was in the military, I encountered something. It was winter, and the snow in the Northeast was knee-deep. Conditions were harsh, and we didn't have enough cotton-padded clothes. People were numb from the cold, and our steps slowed down involuntarily..."

"But it was actually very dangerous. I fell behind. In the icy world, everything was white, the sky was darkening, and there was only that black pine forest..."

Bai Linlin listened, mesmerized, and pattered over to look up at the old man.

"Chirp chirp!"

[And then?]

Song Zheng-guo smiled at the memory of that miraculous experience and said:

"A deer walked over. Its antlers were glowing with a golden light. I had almost lost all sensation, but as soon as it approached... my body became warm."

"Later, my consciousness became blurred. I vaguely felt it was a young boy, holding my hand and leading me... until I woke up surrounded by my comrades..."

Bai Linlin thought it was amazing that it could even lead the way. He forgot that he was a yokai himself and just looked up, urging him on:

"Chirp chirp!"

[Continue, continue!]

Song Zheng-guo’s tone became very peaceful. "My comrades didn't believe me when I told them, because in their eyes, I had walked there myself."

"Later, I asked the local hunters, and they called this kind of creature..."

"A Mountain God."

-

Inside the Bureau.

The Red-Crowned Crane had been quite proud to introduce the photo, but the "commissioner" seemed greatly shocked, repeatedly confirming the name of the guardian of 247.

It could only point below the photo.

Isn't it written right there?

[Song Yu]

The Taoist closed his eyes, unwilling to face reality. Later, the old man held up a finger and made a request:

"I need to check this yokai's file."

Although the Red-Crowned Crane was a bit puzzled, it was confident. Check it then!

Every yokai in their Bureau was a good one!

But just then, a weary sigh came from behind:

"Who on earth taught you to take photos like this... and with a red background, no less..."

-

The file check was actually a bit bumpy because the Taoist raised a question:

"In July, its yokai power was registered as F-rank."

"How did it reach A-rank by the end of August? Is that compliant?"

The Red-Crowned Crane: "..."

It knew 247 would cause trouble for it sooner or later.

Taking shortcuts.

"Did it eat people!"

The Taoist’s expression was very serious; he felt there was a major problem, especially since this yokai should... still be at his old friend’s house.

The Red-Crowned Crane closed its eyes and explained:

"No, it’s an F-rank bird. It would struggle to even gnaw on a human finger. It used the yokai power subsidies of other yokai to level up quickly..."

The Taoist finally found the issue and demanded:

"Aren't yokai power subsidies limited to one per yokai? How can they be stacked?"

"There is definitely something wrong!"

"This number 247 must be transferred to the 749 Bureau for inspection."

The Red-Crowned Crane was furious and slammed its wing on the table:

"Stop putting on airs!"

"If it has no problems, it has no problems! If you don't believe me, I'll go with you. It’s only eight months old, not even a year old yet. Can it even eat your finger!"

The Taoist was of the same mind:

"Let's go then!"

-

At Jinyuan, everything was peaceful.

Bai Linlin eventually tried transforming. He stood in the study, looking a bit dazed, and said:

"I actually don't know how to do anything."

"I only just learned how to transform."

Song Zheng-guo smiled and said:

"Just call me Grandfather."

The bird was shy and put his hands behind his back.

"In that case, I can certainly buy the bird a gold bracelet."

Bai Linlin lowered his head, his face flushing red. He felt quite embarrassed. He had only shown off for a moment before immediately turning back into a round little bird.

But just then, there was urgent knocking at the door downstairs.

Song Zheng-guo frowned and stood up to check the situation. The bird had nothing else to do, so it flapped its wings and landed on the man’s shoulder.

About a minute later.

The front door opened.

chunks.chineseText:
外面站着一个奇装异服的道士，以及一个系着藏蓝色丝带的女士，两个人均是臭脸。

“平云？”

宋峥国其实是有些意外的，怎么不说一声就……

道士一眼就看到了老友肩头的鸟，大声地道：

“小妖！”

或许是过于直白，白粼粼直接愣住了，对方抬手就要过来拿他。

鸟直接扑棱翅膀飞走了，站在不远处的地板上，有些懵懵的。

什么情况？

这个时候旁边那位系着丝带的女士抬手就是一拍，硬生生把那个道士的胳膊弄到了玄关的墙壁上，木板都裂开了点。

丹顶鹤不满道：

“干什么呢！它才八个月！”

道士着急地同宋峥国解释：“峥国，这东西是个妖怪，小郁肯定是被他哄骗了！”

“我今天一定要帮你处理了！”

丹顶鹤真是要气死了。

“你再说！”

眼看一人一鹤要掐起来。

并且已经进门了。

白粼粼头脑风暴中，立即开始装傻，鸟眼均匀地往外瞥，翅膀半伸着，爪子也一瘸一拐的。

“啾……啾啾……”

好一个智障小鸟。

门口这会儿的动静也停了，道士蹙眉看了过来，有点嫌弃道：

“这是个笨的？”

不过就在这时，楼上有门开合的动静，有一道很冷的声音传了过来：

“为什么围着我的小鸟？”

玄关那处更安静了。

“粼粼，过来。”

[鸽子][鸽子]：糟糕，有坏人（bushi

Standing outside was a Taoist in strange attire and a lady wearing a navy blue silk ribbon. Both of them had sour expressions.

"Pingyun?"

Song Zheng-guo was actually quite surprised. Why come without even a word...

The Taoist immediately spotted the bird on his old friend’s shoulder and shouted:

"A little demon!"

Perhaps it was too blunt; Bai Linlin was stunned. The man raised his hand, intending to grab him.

The bird flapped its wings and flew away, landing on the floor not far off, looking a bit bewildered.

What was going on?

At this moment, the lady with the silk ribbon raised her hand and struck, forcing the Taoist’s arm against the wall of the entryway so hard that the wood cracked.

The Red-Crowned Crane said indignantly:

"What are you doing! It’s only eight months old!"

The Taoist anxiously explained to Song Zheng-guo: "Zheng-guo, this thing is a yokai. Xiao Yu must have been deceived by it!"

"I must deal with it for you today!"

The Red-Crowned Crane was absolutely furious.

"Say that again!"

Seeing the human and the crane about to clash.

And they had already entered the house.

Bai Linlin was brainstorming. He immediately started playing dumb, his bird eyes darting around, his wings half-extended, and his gait limping.

"Chirp... chirp chirp..."

What a mentally challenged little bird.

The commotion at the door stopped. The Taoist frowned as he looked over, saying with some disdain:

"Is this one a simpleton?"

However, just then, there was the sound of a door opening and closing upstairs, and a very cold voice came down:

"Why are you surrounding my little bird?"

The entryway went even quieter.

"Linlin, come here."

chunks.chineseText:
第41章

地板上的蓝羽小鸟本来还是保持一个奇形怪状的站姿的，但是一听到楼上的声音后立马仰着鸟头看过去了。

人！

白粼粼直接一个扭头起飞，扑棱翅膀还有点着急，爪子都在地板上打了个滑，但最终顺顺利利地抵达宋郁的肩头。

挺胸抬头。

楼下的两人一鹤看后都是一阵沉默，道士尤为生气，觉得自己被欺骗了，伸着手就对宋峥国道：

“你看看你看看！这小妖鬼精鬼精的！”

宋郁面色冷白，抬步直接走下来了，尽管精神还是有些不济，但在玄关口的时候直直地盯着那个穿着道袍的人，面无表情的。

道士：“……”

宋峥国见状连忙道：“小郁，这位是爷爷的朋友，”

道士见状也是松开了和丹顶鹤的纠缠的手，整理了下自己的衣冠，站好了。

多少年没见过了。

“摆什么谱？切。”

门口的那位“女士”环着手臂就冷哼了一声。

宋郁抬眼看了过去，感觉有些熟悉的气质，但又辨别不出来。

“这位……爷爷也不知道。”

宋峥国其实也觉得棘手，毕竟一开门，对面这两个人就在吵，连介绍环节都没有，在玄关口就干起来了。

老人看了下自家的门框。

居然已经裂开了。

宋峥国只是觉得荒谬，这位“女士”……她这么力大无穷？

丹顶鹤在门口站着，心道监护人认不出来就算了，247总不能认不出来吧？

好歹也是个A级妖怪了。

但是它等了好一会，甚至还特地给了宋郁肩头那只一个眼神，上下扫视了下，咳嗽一声，然后再撇开视线。

丹顶鹤认为这再明显不过了。

然而，少年肩头的那只圆滚滚的蓝羽小鸟只是一个劲地歪头看，爪子还活动了下，仿佛是觉得看不太清楚，试图往前凑一凑鸟头，但一个重心不稳，开始一顿扑棱翅膀。

“……”

最后还是宋郁抬手给接住了。

蓝羽小鸟这才重新回了原来位置，收了收翅膀，假装一切事情都没发生。

玄关这里保持着沉默。

丹顶鹤闭了闭眼，深吸一口气，它就知道不能对247抱有任何希望。

于是抬手伸了过去。

它的掌心金纹涌动，在双方面对面的空间里形成了一道“墙”，透明的，但这些宋峥国看不到，丹顶鹤有意避开了。

至于宋郁和肩头的某只，则是在短暂的晃眼之后，看清楚了对面的真实情况。

一个道士，一个……脖子伸得很长的丹顶鹤。

宋郁觉得自己真是烧得不轻。

“啾啾！”

肩头上的小鸟叫声微微唤醒了他，人这才反应过来，是管理局的丹顶鹤。

不过想到这里，宋郁蹙了蹙眉。

怎么，要家访？

他的小鸟最近表现很好的。

“小郁认识吗？”

最后还是宋峥国又问了一句，打破了玄关这里死一般的沉寂。

对面的道士闻言也眯了眯眼，耐心地等着，不过少年没有任何犹豫，只是很平静地道：

“爷爷，这是我的朋友。”

肩头上的小鸟毛绒绒的，很自然地用头拱了拱人的下巴。

“啾！”

-

最后成功地进了门。

不过是分成两组，道士坚持要和宋郁单独谈谈，丹顶鹤则是看中了宋峥国这个老头子。

白粼粼夹在中间窝窝囊囊的，最后还是丹顶鹤挥了挥手，很嫌弃地道：

“跟着你监护人吧。”

鸟如愿以偿地上了宋郁的肩头。

地点分别是一楼的茶室与二楼的书房。

宋峥国听到“监护人”这三个字其实愣了下，心里再三思考，最终还是不得不承认……那可能是说的是小郁。

丹顶鹤优雅地道：“走吧，我们聊聊。”

最终老人选择的地点是茶室，他拉开门，让那位“女士”进来，顺带给沏了一杯热茶。

丹顶鹤端坐在红木椅子上，抬手抿了一口，随后看向这个老头子。

监护人的长辈。

247现在的身份已经趋近于暴露了。

它眯了眯眼，索性直接问道：

“是这样，你觉得那个臭道士说的话是真的吗？”

宋峥国：“……”

他已经见过了，这否认也似乎没有意义，老人皱了皱眉，只是也拿起一杯茶，转而反问道：

“你同鸟儿认识？”

丹顶鹤心想这不废话，它思考了一下，直接变回了本体，用翅膀托着那杯冒着热气的茶，很优雅地整理了下自己脖子上的丝巾。

看向对面的老人。

很矜贵的样子。

宋峥国甚至刚喝完一口茶，一抬眼直接愣住了，整个人的大脑皮层都变得光滑，最后直接呛住了，开始一个劲地咳嗽。

“咳咳咳……不、不好意思。”

老头儿侧头拿了纸巾，对着椅子旁边的一只鹤道歉。

宋峥国其实对于家养的鸟儿确实接受度高些，一来鸟儿本体就很可爱，毛绒绒的，还会穿小披风……就算是化形了，看着也还是个孩子模样。

而面前的……是鹤。

“没关系，人类是有些大惊小怪的。”

丹顶鹤仍然端庄，拿起茶杯又浅浅地啜饮了一口。

鸟类的羽毛就是最好看的部分，人类为此而感到惊艳再正常不过，它可以给这位监护人的长辈一些时间适应。

宋峥国咳嗽了一会，深呼吸一口，然后闭了闭眼，再次回头看了下，那只一米六高的大型涉禽还在坐着，脖子上系着人类的丝带。

它注意到了目光还看了过来，一幅宽容怜悯的样子。

没见识的人类。

宋峥国重新转回了头，再度闭眼，没事的，没事的。

不过是一只会说人话的国家一级保护动物而已。

而已……

-

与此同时。

宋郁已经去了书房，很客气地先开了门，他肩头的小鸟从头到尾都是紧紧贴着他的脖子的，羽毛很是蓬松，成为一个毛球了。

它吓到了。

这位道士跨着四方步走了进来，甚至都还没有坐下，就想回过头来说教，但是被打断了——

“您贵姓？”

宋郁抬手关上了门，出声问道，语气平直且没有起伏，只是很客气地询问。

“……叫我李爷爷就行。”

道士其实也是有些慨叹，当年见到这孩子的时候还那么小，现在居然长这么高了。

就是看着有点脾气不好。

干巴巴的老头摇了摇头。

宋郁身高已经将近一米八五，再加上前些日子健身，肩宽背直的，那张偏冷的脸直接褪去了些“青涩感”，取而代之的是一种密不透风的压迫。

“您先坐。”

这道声音疏离又很寡淡。

道士闻言收了收袖子，的确拉开椅子坐下了，见到对面这孩子也入座了，这才开始单刀直入地道：

“你这小鸟，它是个妖怪！”

宋郁闻言一顿，随即抬眼看了过来，扯唇笑了下，很是不在意道：

“那又如何？”

-

一楼茶室。

丹顶鹤端坐在椅子上，翅膀托着茶杯，观察了下旁边的人类，开始娓娓道来：
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 41

The little blue-feathered bird on the floor had been standing in a rather bizarre posture, but the moment it heard the sounds from upstairs, it immediately tilted its head to look up.

Humans!

Bai Linlin turned and took flight in one motion. It was a bit flustered, its wings flapping in a panic, and its claws even slipped on the floor, but it eventually landed successfully on Song Yu’s shoulder.

It puffed out its chest and held its head high.

The two men and one crane downstairs fell into a silence. The Taoist priest was particularly incensed, feeling as though he had been deceived. He gestured toward Song Zhengguo and exclaimed:

"Look at that! Look! This little demon is craftier than a fox!"

Song Yu’s face was deathly pale. He walked down the stairs, and although his spirit was still somewhat drained, he stared straight at the man in the Taoist robe as he reached the entryway, his expression devoid of emotion.

The Taoist: "..."

Seeing this, Song Zhengguo quickly interjected, "Xiao Yu, this is a friend of your grandfather’s."

The Taoist, seeing the situation, loosened his grip on the red-crowned crane and straightened his robes, standing tall.

It had been so many years since they last met.

"What are you posturing for? Tch."

The "lady" at the door crossed her arms and snorted coldly.

Song Yu looked over, feeling a sense of familiarity with her temperament, yet he couldn't quite place it.

"This... even Grandfather doesn't know."

Song Zhengguo actually found the situation quite thorny. After all, the moment he opened the door, these two were already bickering; they hadn't even gone through introductions before they started scuffling in the entryway.

The old man glanced at his door frame.

It had actually cracked.

Song Zhengguo found it absurd. This "lady"... was she really that incredibly strong?

The red-crowned crane stood at the door, thinking to itself that even if the guardian didn't recognize it, 247 shouldn't be that oblivious, right?

It was, after all, an A-rank demon.

But it waited for quite a while, even pointedly giving the bird on Song Yu’s shoulder a look, scanning it up and down, coughing once, and then looking away.

The red-crowned crane thought it couldn't be more obvious.

However, the round, blue-feathered bird on the youth’s shoulder simply kept tilting its head, wiggling its claws as if it couldn't see clearly and trying to nudge its head forward. It lost its center of gravity and began flapping its wings in a flurry.

"..."

In the end, Song Yu reached out and caught it.

The little blue bird returned to its original position, tucked its wings, and pretended that nothing had happened.

Silence reigned in the entryway.

The red-crowned crane closed its eyes and took a deep breath. It knew better than to hold any hope for 247.

So, it reached out.

Golden patterns surged in its palm, forming a "wall" in the space between the two parties. It was transparent, but Song Zhengguo couldn't see it; the crane had intentionally avoided him.

As for Song Yu and the creature on his shoulder, after a brief moment of dizziness, they saw the reality of the situation across from them.

A Taoist priest, and... a red-crowned crane with a very long neck.

Song Yu felt that his fever must be quite severe.

"Chirp chirp!"

The chirping of the little bird on his shoulder slightly roused him, and he finally realized it was the red-crowned crane from the Management Bureau.

However, thinking of this, Song Yu frowned.

What, was this a home visit?

His little bird had been behaving very well lately.

"Do you know them, Xiao Yu?"

In the end, it was Song Zhengguo who spoke again, breaking the deathly silence of the entryway.

The Taoist across from them squinted, waiting patiently, but the youth didn't hesitate, simply saying calmly:

"Grandfather, this is my friend."

The little bird on his shoulder was fluffy, and it naturally nudged the man’s chin with its head.

"Chirp!"

-

They successfully made it inside.

However, they split into two groups. The Taoist insisted on speaking with Song Yu alone, while the red-crowned crane took a liking to the old man, Song Zhengguo.

Bai Linlin was caught in the middle, feeling quite miserable. In the end, the red-crowned crane waved its hand and said with clear disdain:

"Go follow your guardian."

The bird got its wish and landed on Song Yu’s shoulder.

The locations were the first-floor tea room and the second-floor study.

Song Zhengguo was actually stunned when he heard the word "guardian." He pondered it over and over, finally having to admit... it probably referred to Xiao Yu.

The red-crowned crane said elegantly, "Let’s go, let’s have a chat."

The old man chose the tea room. He opened the door, let the "lady" in, and brewed a pot of hot tea.

The red-crowned crane sat upright on a mahogany chair, took a sip, and then looked at the old man.

The guardian’s elder.

247’s identity was now nearing exposure.

It narrowed its eyes and decided to ask directly:

"So, do you think what that stinking Taoist said is true?"

Song Zhengguo: "..."

He had already seen it; denying it seemed pointless. The old man frowned, picked up his own cup of tea, and countered:

"Are you acquainted with the bird?"

The red-crowned crane thought, *What a foolish question.* It pondered for a moment, then transformed back into its true form. It held the steaming cup of tea with its wings and elegantly adjusted the silk scarf around its neck.

It looked at the old man across from it.

It looked quite noble.

Song Zhengguo had just taken a sip of tea, and when he looked up, he froze. His brain felt like it had gone smooth, and he ended up choking, coughing uncontrollably.

"Cough, cough, cough... I, I apologize."

The old man turned his head to grab a tissue, apologizing to a crane sitting next to the chair.

Song Zhengguo was actually quite accepting of pet birds; for one, the bird’s true form was very cute, fluffy, and it even wore a little cape... even when it transformed, it still looked like a child.

But what was in front of him... was a crane.

"It’s fine. Humans are prone to making a fuss."

The red-crowned crane remained dignified, picking up the teacup to take another shallow sip.

Bird feathers were the most beautiful part of nature; it was perfectly normal for humans to be stunned by them. It could give this guardian’s elder some time to adapt.

Song Zhengguo coughed for a while, took a deep breath, and closed his eyes. When he looked back again, that 1.6-meter-tall large wading bird was still sitting there, wearing a human silk ribbon around its neck.

It noticed his gaze and looked over with a tolerant, pitying expression.

Ignorant human.

Song Zhengguo turned his head away again and closed his eyes. *It’s fine, it’s fine.*

It’s just a nationally protected animal that can speak human language.

Just...

-

Meanwhile.

Song Yu had already gone to the study. He opened the door politely, and the little bird on his shoulder had been pressed tightly against his neck the entire time, its feathers puffed up into a ball.

It was frightened.

The Taoist walked in with a measured, square-stepping gait. Before he could even sit down, he wanted to turn around and lecture, but he was interrupted—

"What is your surname?"

Song Yu closed the door and asked, his tone flat and devoid of inflection, merely inquiring politely.

"...Just call me Grandpa Li."

The Taoist was actually feeling a bit sentimental. When he first saw this child, he was so small, and now he had grown so tall.

It was just that he seemed to have a bit of a temper.

The withered old man shook his head.

Song Yu was nearly 1.85 meters tall, and thanks to his recent fitness routine, his shoulders were broad and his back straight. That cold face had shed its "youthful" look, replaced by a dense, impenetrable sense of pressure.

"Please, sit."

The voice was distant and indifferent.

The Taoist pulled in his sleeves and sat down. Seeing the boy across from him also take a seat, he went straight to the point:

"This little bird of yours, it’s a demon!"

Song Yu paused, then looked up, curled his lips into a smile, and said with complete indifference:

"And so what?"

-

In the tea room on the first floor.

The red-crowned crane sat upright on the chair, holding the teacup with its wings, observing the human beside it, and began to speak at length:

chunks.chineseText:
“相信你也能看出来，我们247它就是一个小鸟，它当时在秋水巷的一家花鸟小店里，天可怜见，自生出来就没有父母陪着的，才五个月大就被你们孩子给带走了。”

宋峥国眼皮微微抽了下，但还是莫名紧张了起来，搓了搓手，道：

“是，鸟儿确实还很小，是我们小郁早早地把它带过来的，应该负责。”

丹顶鹤闻言还算满意，微微点了点头，随即又道：
